items.title: Artisanat : l'Exécutif reconnaît les difficultés de paiement des cotisations à l’AMO
items.description: Avec près de 2,7 millions de professionnels, soit environ 22 % de la population active, l’artisanat occupe une place importante dans le tissu économique marocain. Pourtant, l’accès à la protection sociale demeure problématique pour une partie des artisans, dont certains peinent à honorer leurs cotisations mensuelles. Une difficulté reconnue par Abdeljebbar Rachidi, ministre délégué chargé de l’Artisanat et de l’Économie sociale et solidaire, lors de la séance hebdomadaire des questions orales à la Chambre des conseillers. Le responsable gouvernemental a expliqué que plusieurs artisans avaient bien été inscrits au régime de couverture médicale, sans toutefois parvenir à maintenir leur affiliation. L’interruption du paiement des cotisations a ainsi conduit à la suspension de leur déclaration dans le Registre national de l’artisanat. Parmi les facteurs à l’origine de cette situation, il a notamment cité les transitions entre les régimes « AMO Achamil » et « AMO Tadamon », ainsi que les liens entre le statut de certains bénéficiaires et le dispositif de l’aide sociale directe. Face à ces difficultés, le gouvernement travaille à une révision du système de l’aide sociale directe. Des campagnes de sensibilisation sont également prévues afin d’inciter les artisans à maintenir leur adhésion au système de protection sociale et à tirer pleinement profit des prestations auxquelles il donne accès. Au-delà de la question de la couverture médicale, le secteur reste confronté à des contraintes structurelles qui pèsent sur son activité. La hausse des prix des matières premières figure parmi les principales préoccupations des professionnels. Pour y faire face, le ministère mise notamment sur la distribution de laine, la mise à niveau des tanneries et la conclusion de conventions permettant aux artisans de s’approvisionner en matières premières à des tarifs préférentiels. Le ministre a également plaidé pour le développement de la production locale de ces matières, à travers des partenariats entre les secteurs public et privé. L'enjeu est de réduire les coûts de production tout en améliorant les conditions de travail des artisans. © Mounir Mehimdate Le renforcement des infrastructures constitue un autre axe de l'action ministérielle. Le Maroc dispose actuellement d'environ 130 structures dédiées à la production et à la commercialisation, auxquelles s'ajoutent 110 maisons de l'artisane implantées en milieu rural. Ces dernières bénéficient à quelque 3.900 femmes. Le département entend désormais faire évoluer la vocation de ces espaces pour les transformer en unités de production et de commercialisation, mais aussi en plateformes régionales d'appui à l'artisanat. La préservation de l'identité des produits nationaux figure également parmi les priorités affichées par le ministère. Concernant les salons professionnels, Abdeljebbar Rachidi a fait état de cahiers des charges destinés à garantir le respect des spécificités de l'artisanat marocain et à éviter que des produits étrangers, notamment asiatiques, ne soient présentés aux côtés des productions nationales dans les manifestations consacrées à l'artisanat marocain. Cette démarche passe aussi par le développement de labels de qualité, à l'image de « Made in Morocco », ainsi que des labels régionaux et collectifs. Ces dispositifs doivent permettre de mieux identifier les produits artisanaux, de valoriser leur origine et de prévenir toute confusion avec d'autres marchandises. Sur le terrain de l'ouverture des marchés, le programme « Maroc Export » a reçu 543 candidatures, dont 135 relevant du secteur de l'artisanat, selon les chiffres communiqués par le ministre. Le département travaille parallèlement à la mise en place de programmes d'accompagnement des groupements de producteurs et des exportateurs, ainsi que de dispositifs d'excellence destinés aux filières du tapis, de la poterie et de la céramique. © Mounir Mehimdate Au total, 104 bénéficiaires ont profité de l'accompagnement destiné aux groupements de producteurs, tandis que 141 autres ont bénéficié d'un appui à l'exportation. Ces programmes visent à consolider les compétences des opérateurs et à renforcer la compétitivité des produits artisanaux sur les marchés. Enfin, le ministre a évoqué l'organisation de la Coupe du monde comme une occasion de promouvoir l'identité et le patrimoine marocains. Un rendez-vous international dont le pays entend tirer parti pour mettre en avant la diversité et la richesse de son artisanat, ainsi que les dimensions culturelles et civilisationnelles qui le caractérisent. The post Artisanat : l'Exécutif reconnaît les difficultés de paiement des cotisations à l’AMO appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Spain coach optimistic over Yamal’s fitness for England Nations League clash
items.description: Spain coach Luis de la Fuente said Wednesday he is optimistic Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal will be fit to face England in the Nations League at the weekend. The 19-year-old winger will miss the world champions’ visit to face the Czech Republic in Prague on Thursday with a knee problem and is set to join up with Spain after that game. Yamal played for Barcelona in the 2-1 La Liga win over Atletico Madrid on Sunday and on Monday Spain said he would not travel to face the Czechs. “He got hurt in the last match, he had some discomfort in one knee, he went for the usual treatment, a scan in Barcelona, and they saw he had inflammation and fluid in the knee — that meant he needed rest,” De la Fuente told reporters. “Our medical staff and his medical staff have a fantastic relationship, and I decided that his trip here should be avoided without knowing whether he’d be in any condition to play.” The coach said he had spoken to the winger and his recovery was looking positive ahead of England’s visit to Madrid on Sunday. “He’s doing a series of exercises with his physio and with the club that indicate the recovery is going well,” continued De la Fuente. “We believe, I’m optimistic, that on Friday he’ll be with us.” De la Fuente dismissed the idea that Yamal, who came third in the Ballon d’Or voting in October, has any special privileges compared to his La Roja team-mates. “He has no privileges, and his team-mates are relaxed about it, because we treat everyone the same,” added the coach. “In similar situations we would have done exactly the same for any other player, and the players know that.” – Unstoppable run – Spain have won all four games so far in Group A3 and sealed qualification to the quarter-finals. De la Fuente’s side are unbeaten in their last 43 competitive outings, and the coach said it provided his team with extra motivation. “We want to keep setting new milestones, and this is another one,” explained De la Fuente. “None of us would probably ever have thought we’d even reach 35, because we already felt those were astronomical numbers, but having reached 43, you think, my goodness, we want to get to 44, of course we do.” Spain won their previous outing away in Croatia with a brace from Arsenal’s Mikel Merino. The midfielder is frequently used as a substitute by De la Fuente to great effect, with Merino netting vital goals against Portugal and Belgium in the World Cup off the bench this summer. Merino said he would like to be a starter for Spain but he would not kick up a fuss. “Of course, what player wouldn’t like to get (more) minutes?” Merino told reporters. “You’ll never hear me complain about the coach’s decision, I will respect it… but all players want to be important, have minutes and enjoy themselves on the pitch.” The post Spain coach optimistic over Yamal’s fitness for England Nations League clash appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ahead of 2027 Budget: Techiman drivers complain about fuel prices as traders lament slow sales and delays in Women’s Development Bank
items.description: As Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson prepares to present the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy to Parliament tomorrow, Thursday, November 12, at 6:00 pm, the mood in Techiman reflects a mixture of hope and frustration. The budget is expected to outline the government’s “New Economy Agenda” – a strategic shift from economic stabilisation to productivity, competitiveness, job creation and infrastructure development. It is also expected to include plans to fully fund the Accra-Kumasi Expressway using oil revenues. The government has promised not to introduce new taxes, opting instead for expenditure rationalisation and spending cuts. However, at the Techiman Central Market and the main lorry terminals, residents say their concerns go beyond policy documents, as they look forward to measures that will provide tangible relief. Drivers: Fuel prices are squeezing us For drivers who ply the busy Techiman-Kumasi-Kintampo routes, the rising cost of fuel remains their biggest concern. “Fuel prices keep going up every week,” one driver at the main terminal said. “Every time we hear there’s a budget, we pray it brings relief. The government must do something about fuel prices – that’s our biggest problem. If fuel goes up, everything goes up for us.” Another driver appealed for stability in fuel prices. “We are not asking for too much. Just stabilise fuel prices so we can plan. When fuel is high, passengers complain, and we also suffer. The budget should address this,” he said. Market women: Goods are available, but buyers say there’s no money At the Techiman Central Market, traders said prices of goods had remained relatively stable, but sales were slow because, according to them, customers had little money to spend. “The goods are here, prices haven’t changed much, but nobody is buying,” one trader lamented. “Customers keep telling us there’s no money. How do we survive like this?” she asked. Disappointment over Women’s Development Bank Several market women also expressed disappointment over the delay in rolling out the government’s proposed Women’s Development Bank, which they expected would provide access to affordable loans to expand their businesses. “We were promised the Women’s Development Bank. We voted for it. We waited for it. Where is it?” one trader asked. “If that bank had come, we would have accessed soft loans to expand our businesses. We are disappointed,” she added. Hope for tomorrow Despite their frustrations, many traders said they were looking forward to the budget with cautious optimism. “Tomorrow we will listen to the budget. We want to hear something for the ordinary trader,” one market woman said. “No new taxes is good, but we need real support – affordable credit and a market that moves,” she added. Others believe investment in infrastructure could help ease their challenges. “If they fix the roads, it helps us. Our goods travel from Accra, from Kumasi. Good roads mean lower transport costs. That would be something,” another trader said. What to expect from the 2027 Budget The budget is expected to focus on the government’s “New Economy Agenda”, with an emphasis on moving from economic stabilisation to productivity, competitiveness, job creation and infrastructure development. It is also expected to outline plans for funding the Accra-Kumasi Expressway with oil revenues, while the government has pledged not to introduce new taxes and instead rely on expenditure rationalisation and spending cuts. Dr Ato Forson is scheduled to present the budget to Parliament on Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 6:00 pm. For the people of Techiman, the budget is more than a policy document; it is a test of promises made and expectations yet to be fulfilled. “We are watching,” one driver said. “We voted for change. Tomorrow, we will listen carefully. The budget must speak to our pockets.”

items.title: Burkina : Une session ministérielle fait le bilan de la feuille de route de l'An II de la confédération AES
items.description: Le Burkina Faso accueille, les 11 et 12 novembre 2026, la session du conseil des ministres de la confédération de l'Alliance des États du Sahel (AES). Les travaux, ouverts ce mercredi 11 novembre sous la présidence du ministre d'État, ministre de la défense, Célestin Simporé, portent sur l'examen de la mise en œuvre de la feuille de route de l'An II de la confédération. L'objectif de cette rencontre ministérielle qui réunit les délégations du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger est de faire le point sur les activités réalisées et de définir les prochaines orientations de la confédération de l'Alliance des États du Sahel. Pendant deux jours, les participants passeront en revue les actions menées dans les trois domaines prioritaires de l'AES : la défense et la sécurité, la diplomatie et le développement. Cette session ministérielle vise également à préparer la prochaine rencontre du collège des chefs d'État de la confédération. À cet effet, les ministres devront dresser le bilan des activités inscrites dans la feuille de route de l'An II, formuler des recommandations sur la poursuite du processus et examiner diverses autres questions. Sur le volet défense et sécurité, le ministre a insisté sur la nécessité de poursuivre la mutualisation des moyens, notamment en matière de renseignement, et de renforcement de l'autonomie stratégique des États membres. Il a rappelé le rôle des forces armées nationales et de la force conjointe de l'AES dans la lutte contre les menaces sécuritaires. La photo de famille Sur le plan diplomatique, il a mis en avant la volonté des trois pays de porter une voix commune sur la scène internationale, tout en diversifiant leurs partenariats sur la base de leurs intérêts nationaux et confédéraux. Quant au pilier développement, il a souligné la nécessité de renforcer l'intégration économique, de faciliter les échanges commerciaux et de valoriser les ressources naturelles des trois pays. Selon lui, ces actions doivent contribuer à créer des perspectives économiques durables, notamment pour la jeunesse. À l'issue des travaux, une note de synthèse est attendue. Ce document devra présenter les principales avancées enregistrées dans chacun des trois piliers et faire ressortir les efforts accomplis au cours de cette deuxième année de la confédération. Pour Célestin Simporé, cette rencontre ne constitue pas une simple formalité administrative, mais un cadre d'évaluation stratégique destiné à consolider les acquis et à définir les prochaines étapes de la construction de l'espace AES. Au-delà de l'examen de la mise en œuvre de la feuille de route de l'An II de la confédération, le ministre Simporé a abordé certaines questions d'actualité. Pour lui, la question des Burkinabè orpailleurs expulsés de la Guinée, qui soulève des enjeux humanitaires, a mis en évidence la solidarité entre les peuples de l'AES. Il a, à cet effet, exprimé sa reconnaissance aux autorités maliennes pour leur accompagnement dans la gestion de cette situation. Le ministre de la défense a, au nom des participants, présenté ses condoléances au président du Niger, Abdourahamane Tiani, qui a perdu son père. Rama Diallo Lefaso.net

items.title: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
items.description: Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain’s first general strike for 14 years, called by the country’s main unions over housing and the high cost of living. Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas. Transport and other public services across Spain faced serious disruption. Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November. The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with “massive” participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was “very significant.” There was a heavy police presence in the centre of Barcelona on Wednesday evening, with officers wearing helmets and riot shields. Some of the disturbances took place in the Passeig de Gràcia, close to the iconic Plaça de Catalunya in the centre of the city. Small fires burned in the middle of the streets as bins were set alight. Local media reported that a group of people fired fireworks towards police and looted shops including the Lego store. Protesters were also seen trying to enter the Apple Store. The BBC spoke to a woman who attended the protests in Barcelona who said it was mostly very peaceful and “joyful”. She said she was there to protest about the housing costs and that “there were a lot of children and old people there.” She was in the area of Las Ramblas in the evening and saw fires in the streets. “The fires were everywhere, it was very intense,” she said. Earlier in the day there was major disruption around Madrid and Barcelona, with traffic halted on several main roads. The interior ministry said dozens of people were arrested for a variety of incidents and Spanish reports said estate agencies had seen attacks on their offices. “We’ve completely brought the city to a standstill,” a protester in Madrid told Reuters news agency, adding there was widespread support for the general strike. “Everyone’s out there, despite the rainy weather; everyone’s out on the streets.” Another protester, 37-year-old teacher Olga Domingo, said she was protesting because “the housing situation is outrageous. The current cost of living compared to wages is completely unsustainable”. The strike was triggered by widespread protests over affordable housing and rising living costs, after the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from a flat in Madrid where she had lived for seven decades. She died in hospital weeks later. Rental prices in the capital have risen in recent years. The monthly cost of a 50 sq m apartment in Madrid was an average of €1,170 ($1,300; £1,000) in October, according to property portal Idealista, while Spain’s average gross monthly salary is about €2,460. That amounts to nearly half the average gross salary, well above the 30% level of affordability often recommended by housing experts and public institutions.Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called snap elections last month after parliament failed to approve his plan for housing reform. Not since 2012, under the conservative government of Mariano Rajoy, has Spain held general strikes. And while previous strikes have been problematic for the government in power, this one is different. Sánchez and his ministers have even encouraged workers to down tools and demand affordable housing. “Your eight-hour day. Your pension. Your public healthcare… These were collective conquests,” he wrote on social media, praising those who took part in previous strikes. Tyres were set on fire in the city of Gijon in northern Spain The conservative People’s Party (PP), by contrast, has accused the government of attempting to weaponise the strike for electoral gain. PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo called the general strike “nonsense”, calling the unions “mafia” and “trash”. Feijoo’s party is leading in the polls and party spokesman Miguel Tellado accused the government of exploiting the strike to warn voters against allowing a right-wing government to be formed, which looks the most likely outcome of the 29 November election. Sánchez told Spanish TV this week: “What is nonsense is to question the rights of workers to strike.” Among those taking part in the general strike was Gonzalo Álvarez, 27, who was visiting different picket lines in central Madrid. Although he works in sales, he has been volunteering for a housing union that tries to protect tenants and makes them aware of their rights. The eviction of Maricarmen Abascal at the end of September “was the little fire” that sparked this protest, he told the BBC. Álvarez knew the 87-year-old, who had faced a tripling of her rent under new landlords, and says he was deeply upset by her treatment. He rents a small, one-bedroom flat with his girlfriend, a dental hygienist, in the city’s southern Arganzuela disrict. The couple pay €1,000 between them, which means each spends about half of their salary on housing, even before other bills. “It’s absolutely crazy… with the food, with the electricity, with the water, with gas.” He sees no way of getting on the property ladder: “You have to collect an insane amount of money to be able to buy a house. So with these salaries, it’s impossible.” With current rent and purchase prices, he believes buying somewhere is “completely impossible”. Gonzalo Álvarez, who was taking part in the general strike, says 50% of his salary goes towards rent However, the vice-president of the CEOE, Spanish biggest business association, Miguel Garrido, criticised the strike, complaining that businesses had little to do with the price of housing. “This is not a strike for labour-related reasons, but rather for political ones, and it is closely linked to the early calling of elections,” he said. Demonstrations were planned for some of Spain’s biggest cities later in the day and the scale of support will be widely viewed as an indicator of public discontent ahead of the election. Another reliable indicator of support for strikes is the level of demand for electricity with Spain’s industrial sector. Power usage in Spain fell by 7.5% during the early hours of Wednesday, according to data from operator Red Eléctrica. During the last general strike 14 years ago, equivalent consumption was down by more than 15%.

items.title: Vehicle ploughs into pedestrians in Los Angeles, killing three
items.description: An SUV ploughed into a group of pedestrians in the North ​Hollywood district of Los Angeles on Tuesday, killing at least three ‌and critically injuring three more, authorities said. No official details were immediately available about the incident, which happened shortly before 6 p.m. PST (0200 GMT). A police spokesperson said investigators ​had yet to determine if the crash was accidental or ​deliberate. “We need to understand exactly what happened and what led to ⁠this tragedy,” Los Angeles County Supervisor Kathryn Barger said in a ​statement. “I will be closely following the investigation and seeking additional information as the ​facts emerge.” Three people hit by the vehicle were declared dead at the scene, while two pedestrians and the driver of the vehicle were taken to hospitals, the Los ​Angeles police and fire departments said. Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass said the ​SUV drove onto a sidewalk and struck a group of street vendors and pedestrians, ‌adding ⁠that first responders were on the scene and that her office was working closely with city departments. “I’m heartbroken for the families of everyone impacted,” she added on X, promising updates as more information came in. Television station KCAL-TV, ​a CBS News ​affiliate, said a ⁠car crashed into a food stand near a bus stop along Lankershim Boulevard a major road through the busy ​NoHo commercial and arts district in the city’s San ​Fernando Valley. A ⁠small white, partially crumpled SUV appeared to have run up onto the sidewalk under a blue canopy to hit the side of a mass-transit ⁠shelter ​structure, aerial news images from KCAL showed.

items.title: Nvidia is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang, WSJ reports
items.description: Nvidia board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after he had two extramarital affairs, including one with ​a suspected Chinese spy, the Wall Street Journal reported ‌on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter. The board is preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine his future, the report added. Earlier ​in the day, the New York Times reported that Huang ​had an extramarital affair with a company executive who ⁠reported to him. The relationship was with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice ​president of healthcare, the New York Times said, citing five people ​who worked at the company. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Reuters could not immediately verify the reports. The reports on Wednesday come ​days after Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife, as Nvidia’s ​board investigates whether he was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The latest revelation escalates a controversy that has drawn scrutiny from lawmakers, investors, and Nvidia’s board over Huang’s conduct and his relationship with Alice Huang, a woman US intelligence says has facilitated shipments of Nvidia chips to Chinese firms. Nvidia’s shares ⁠were down about 8% in after-hours trading. The stock has lost more than $300 billion in market ​value since news of the affair with Alice ​Huang broke. Huang’s potential exit would create a leadership vacuum at the $4 trillion company, a focal point in the US-China race for AI supremacy, given its dominance in chips used to train models and power services such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT.

items.title: La justice a rendu son verdict dans l’affaire Al-Karama Holding
items.description: La justice a rendu son verdict dans l'affaire de corruption visant le président-directeur général de la société Al Karama Holding et un ancien cadre judiciaire. Ces derniers ont été condamnésn hier par la Chambre criminelle près le tribunal de première instance de Tunis à huit ans de prison ferme, et ce, pour abus de pouvoir, atteinte aux intérêts administratifs et détournement de fonds publics dans l'exercice de leurs fonctions. Dans cette même affaire, un ancien magistrat et de deux autres accusés ont écopé de 3 ans de prison, alors que plusieurs autres prévenus employés d’Al Karama Holding, ont bénéficié d'un non-lieu en faveur de plusieurs autres prévenus, ajoute une source citée par l'agence Tap, ce mercredi 11 novembre 2026. La même source soumogne que les prévenus ont été poursuivis sur la base de l'article 96 du Code pénal, pour des accusations d'abus de pouvoir à des fins d'enrichissement personnel ou de préjudice porté à l'administration, ainsi que d'actes de complicité. items.title: DSS foils major terror plot, intercepts 21 AK-47s, other arms from Niger in Sokoto
items.description: By Soni Daniel, Northern Region Editor Barely 70 days to the the 2027 general elections, the Department of State Security Services has foiled a major terror plot by intercepting a large consignment of high-calibre weapons and ammunition smuggled into the country from Niger Republic. The weapons, including 21 AK-47 rifles, 4 PKT machine guns and 825 magazines, were intercepted exclusively by DSS officers in Dawakawa, Goronyo Local Government Area of Sokoto State, following intensive surveillance of terror cells seeking to transport deadly weapons into Nigeria ahead of the general elections. A security source disclosed that, given increased interception of illegal weapons by the DSS around the country, terror groups have turned to women and beasts of burden, particularly camels, to move illegal weapons into and around the country. It will be recalled that earlier in the week, DSS operatives in Talata Mafaran LGA of Zamfara State, arrested another suspected female arms courier, Hafsat Umar. Umar, who was arrested with 12 grenades and two ammunition belts, is the 14th female illegal arms courier arrested by the DSS between February 2025 and November 2026. Intelligence indicated that the suspected illegal arms courier travelled to Niger State to source ammunition for delivery to a notorious bandit leader, Saidu Marafa, who is based in Kani Kawa, Maradun LGA of Zamfara State. The arrests by the DSS span Zamfara, Nasarawa, Ebonyi, Taraba, Kaduna and Plateau States. Notable among the arrests was that of Aisha Mohammed, apprehended last month in Keffi, Nasarawa State, while allegedly conveying arms and ammunition through a notorious arms dealer and kidnapper simply called Sani. Recovered from Aisha were 202 rounds of 7.62mm AK-47 ammunition and three empty AK-47 magazines. In September, 2026, two female couriers, Chika Aguzie and Blessing Nwamba were arrested at separate locations in Ebonyi State over their alleged involvement in the supply of weapons and explosives to commanders of the outlawed Eastern Security Network (ESN). The commanders include Chinonso Amobi Okafor, aka Temple, and B44, reportedly based in Anambra State. 14 wraps of IED detonators, were recovered during the operation. In August, DSS arrested one Rabiatu Halidu, on Abacha Road, Katu LGA of Nasarawa State with 501 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition. In February, DSS officers arrested one Aisha Ibrahim in Tsafe, LGA of Zamfara State, with 975 rounds of ammunition. Arested in January were Sakina Muhammad and Badariyya Abubakar, along Wukari-Jalingo Road, Taraba State, with one AK-47 rifle, 984 rounds of special ammunition, 105 rounds of GPMG ammunition and 14 empty AK-47 magazines. The Service also recorded several arrests in 2025, including Rahane Sanusi, in Talatan Mafara LGA of Zamfara State. She was caught while conveying ammunition from an illegal arms dealer in Sokoto State to a notorious bandit, Ibrahim Bare, aka Baba, in Anka LGA of the state. Also arrested during the period was Suwaiba Abubakar, Halima Umar, Firdausi Haruna, Saidya Ibrahim and Fatima Sani, with varying quantities of arms and ammunition recovered from them. Recall that, early in the year, the Federal High Court, Abuja, handed convicted some women for terrorism-related cases involving female arms couriers arrested by the DSS. In two instances, three female couriers, identified as Halima Abdullahi, Safiya Salihu and Halima Umar, were convicted and sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment each following their arraignment on terrorism-related charges by the DSS. “Like the others before her,” noted a security source, “Hafsat Umar will also be charged to court, and the DSS will use intelligence at their disposal to bring other criminals to justice.” “The DSS will continue to leverage on actionable intelligence and sustained tactical operations to identify, identify and apprehend all individuals involved in the illegal arms trade and bring them to justice,” declared the source. The post DSS foils major terror plot, intercepts 21 AK-47s, other arms from Niger in Sokoto appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Financement des projets confédéraux : L’AES appelle à la vigilance et réaffirme le rôle central de la BCID-AES
items.description: Face à la multiplication des initiatives privées et associatives de levée de fonds destinées à appuyer la réalisation de projets confédéraux, les gouvernements membres de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES) ont apporté une clarification ferme ce mercredi 11 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Tout en saluant l'élan patriotique et solidaire des peuples du Sahel et des diasporas, les autorités ont publié un communiqué officiel, signé par le porte-parole du gouvernement burkinabè, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo, exigeant une autorisation préalable auprès des Comités nationaux AES pour toute opération de collecte. Exhortant les citoyens à la plus grande vigilance face aux risques de souscriptions frauduleuses, l'AES rappelle que la Banque Confédérale pour l'Investissement et le Développement (BCID-AES) demeure l'unique instrument financier officiel dédié au développement endogène de la région. L'enthousiasme populaire suscité par la construction de l'espace confédéral exige désormais un cadre réglementaire strict. Dans un communiqué conjoint rendu public ce mercredi 11 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou par la voix du ministre Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo, porte-parole du gouvernement du Burkina Faso s'exprimant au nom de ses pairs de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES), les gouvernements ont fait le constat d'une prolifération d'initiatives citoyennes. Des associations, des groupements et des particuliers organisent de manière autonome des collectes de fonds pour soutenir les projets confédéraux. Les autorités de l'AES ont chaleureusement salué cette mobilisation patriotique, y voyant la preuve de la détermination des populations sahéliennes à bâtir un espace fort, souverain et prospère. Toutefois, la noblesse de la cause ne saurait affranchir les initiateurs des exigences de légalité et de traçabilité. Afin de garantir la transparence des opérations et de sécuriser les fonds mobilisés, les gouvernements de l'AES ont rappelé que l'édification de la Confédération doit s'inscrire impérativement dans un cadre institutionnel légal. Désormais, toute personne ou structure souhaitant lancer une campagne de collecte de ressources financières est tenue de se rapprocher des Comités ou Commissions nationaux AES compétents pour obtenir une autorisation préalable obligatoire. Afin d'éviter que la générosité publique ne soit exploitée à des fins malveillantes, les autorités appellent à la prudence. Les gouvernements confédéraux invitent instamment les citoyens des pays membres, les diasporas sahéliennes et africaines, ainsi que tous les partenaires de l'AES à s'abstenir d'effectuer des versements d'argent à des entités dépourvues d'habilitation officielle. De plus, la population est vivement encouragée à signaler sans délai aux autorités compétentes toute tentative suspecte de levée de fonds opérée au nom de la Confédération. Pour centraliser et canaliser l'effort financier vers des réalisations stratégiques, la Confédération rappelle l'existence de son bras financier propre. Le communiqué souligne que l'AES s'est dotée de la Banque Confédérale pour l'Investissement et le Développement de l'AES (BCID-AES). Cet établissement bancaire a pour vocation exclusive de fédérer la mobilisation des ressources financières dans un cadre transparent, garantissant ainsi un développement endogène partagé au bénéfice de l'ensemble des peuples de l'espace confédéral. items.title: Midparc capte la production de joints des Boeing 737 MAX et 777X
items.description: Le groupe suédois Trelleborg transfère vers son usine de Midparc la fabrication de joints d’étanchéité destinés aux Boeing 737 MAX et 777X, un mouvement qui conforte la place de la plateforme casablancaise dans la chaîne des grands avionneurs. Trelleborg Sealing Solutions déplace vers le Royaume la production de joints techniques jusque-là réalisée ailleurs pour deux programmes phares de Boeing, le 737 MAX et le 777X. L’information est rapportée par le média spécialisé allemand Airliners.de, qui précise que cette activité sera assurée par la nouvelle unité du groupe, implantée à Midparc, la zone industrielle de Nouaceur, aux portes de Casablanca. Les pièces concernées entrent dans la construction de plusieurs ensembles de l’appareil, notamment les cellules, les ailes et les nacelles des moteurs. Leur rôle est de garantir l’étanchéité et la fiabilité des avions dans des conditions d’exploitation particulièrement sévères, ce qui explique les exigences de qualification qui pèsent sur ce type de composants. Pour absorber ces volumes, le site casablancais ne part pas de zéro. Il s’appuie sur un laboratoire de matériaux et sur des capacités de fabrication qui couvrent à la fois la transformation de polymères et la production de composants métalliques. Le groupe compte monter en cadence de manière progressive, sur une période de deux ans, avec un dispositif de formation conçu en partenariat avec l’Institut des métiers de l’aéronautique (IMA). L’usine, inaugurée en juin 2026, représente un investissement d’environ 130 millions de dirhams. À terme, elle doit employer entre 150 et 200 personnes, sur des postes qualifiés. Spécialiste mondial des solutions à base de polymères, Trelleborg y exploite son deuxième site de production dans le pays. Lors de la cérémonie d’ouverture, le ministre de l’Industrie et du Commerce, Ryad Mezzour, avait replacé ce projet dans la stratégie des pouvoirs publics visant à relever le taux d’intégration locale de l’aéronautique et à ancrer davantage le Royaume dans les chaînes d’approvisionnement mondiales du secteur. Selon lui, l’arrivée d’un deuxième site du groupe témoigne de la confiance d’un acteur de premier plan et ouvre la voie à un partenariat industriel appelé à se développer. Il avait également estimé que le pays disposait des atouts nécessaires pour devenir une plateforme clé des activités de Trelleborg en Afrique et dans la zone EMEA. Le ministre avait en outre souligné que cette dynamique dépasse le seul périmètre de l’aéronautique. Elle gagne d’autres filières jugées stratégiques, à l’image du transport ferroviaire, de l’ingénierie, de la recherche et développement, des énergies renouvelables ou encore de l’hydrogène vert. Du côté de l’industriel, le PDG de Trelleborg, Peter Nilson, avait présenté cette implantation comme une étape majeure pour le groupe. Elle lui permettra, avait-il expliqué, de mieux accompagner les grands donneurs d’ordre du secteur, parmi lesquels Safran et Airbus, ainsi que d’autres partenaires industriels déjà présents dans le Royaume. Le patron de Midparc, Hamid Benbrahim El Andaloussi, également présent, avait pour sa part jugé que l’arrivée de Trelleborg consoliderait l’écosystème aéronautique national et accompagnerait la prochaine phase de croissance de la filière, avec davantage de technologie, d’innovation et de valeur ajoutée. Ce projet fait suite à un protocole d’accord conclu entre le gouvernement et le groupe suédois en marge du Marrakech Air Show 2024, qui s’était tenu du 30 octobre au 3 novembre. Le transfert de la fabrication de joints destinés à Boeing s’inscrit ainsi dans le prolongement des activités aéronautiques que Trelleborg développe dans le Royaume, et renforce le positionnement de Midparc au sein de la chaîne d’approvisionnement des grands constructeurs internationaux. items.title: Ghana risks being shortchanged in carbon credit deal – Annoh-Dompreh
items.description: Minority Chief Whip Frank Annoh-Dompreh has urged the government to negotiate better prices under Ghana’s proposed carbon credit agreement, warning that the country risks undervaluing its environmental resources. Speaking in Parliament on Wednesday, the Nsawam-Adoagyiri MP questioned a proposed pricing range of US$5 to US$25 per tonne. He contrasted this with what he described as a global average of about US$40 per tonne. He called on the sector minister and negotiating authorities to review the financial terms before Ghana commits to the arrangement. Referring to page eight, paragraph 5.6 of the committee’s report, Mr Annoh-Dompreh said the pricing gap warranted closer scrutiny. He argued that Ghana’s participation in international climate cooperation should help it secure stronger commercial terms. While supporting the agreement’s broader objectives, he cautioned against rushing the financial arrangements at the expense of the country’s long-term interests. The MP acknowledged Ghana’s progress in carbon market cooperation. He cited agreements with Switzerland, Sweden and Singapore, as well as the proposed arrangement with South Korea. He said such partnerships must remain consistent with Ghana’s Nationally Determined Contributions and its commitments under international climate frameworks. Annoh-Dompreh also welcomed provisions linked to the Paris Agreement, particularly opportunities to strengthen capacity and improve environmental management. Beyond pricing, he called for the proposed recovery of methane from landfill sites to cover more facilities across the country. He urged the minister to look beyond the Poon landfill site identified in the report. He cited the landfill at Sumia in his constituency, where he said harmful leachate was destroying plant and animal life. Including more sites, he argued, could help Ghana tackle pollution while generating value through methane recovery and carbon credits. He stressed that the arrangements should deliver practical benefits to affected communities, alongside their commercial and climate objectives. Annoh-Dompreh also pressed the government to bring its carbon credit agreement with British Petroleum (BP) before Parliament. According to him, negotiations had been concluded and the terms reviewed by the Attorney-General. He urged the minister to submit the agreement before the House rose, if the remaining processes could be completed in time. Despite his concerns, the Minority Chief Whip encouraged MPs to support the committee’s report and the agreement. He maintained, however, that securing fair prices and addressing local environmental problems must remain priorities.

items.title: The Politics of Reconciliation: A case for lawyer Kwasi Kwarteng
items.description: As the NPP embarks on the difficult but necessary task of rebuilding party unity, it has an opportunity to demonstrate that unity is not merely a political slogan, but a commitment reflected in deliberate choices, difficult compromises and tangible acts of goodwill. Kwasi Kwarteng, who served as spokesperson for Hon. Kennedy Agyapong during one of the party’s fiercest flagbearership contests, distinguished himself by placing the interests of the NPP above personal allegiance. He promptly embraced Dr. Bawumia’s leadership and has since consistently worked across factional lines to promote reconciliation, even at a time when the party faced the real threat of fragmentation. His subsequent decision not to extend the internal rivalry into the National Communications Director contest, together with his sustained efforts in working for the party, demonstrates a willingness to subordinate personal ambition to the larger interests of the party. It would therefore send a powerful and reassuring message if Dr. Bawumia, the National Executive and the party leadership were to recognise and protect this investment in reconciliation by supporting a consensus arrangement that allows Kwasi Kwarteng to go unopposed in the Asante Akyem North parliamentary primaries. Such a gesture would go beyond the political interests of one individual or constituency. It would reassure disgruntled party members that reconciliation is genuine, demonstrate that loyalty and sacrifices are recognised, and give everyone a renewed sense of belonging in the NPP. It would also be a tangible demonstration to party faithfuls and the Ghanaian public that the NPP has genuinely turned the page, values those who build bridges and are prepared to make practical sacrifices in pursuit of a united political front.

items.title: 17-year-old charged with murder over killing of Ghanaian teenager Javits Frimpong in New York
items.description: A 17-year-old has been charged with murder in connection with the fatal shooting of 15-year-old Ghanaian boy Javits Frimpong in the Bronx, New York. The New York Police Department (NYPD) said detectives arrested the suspect on Wednesday morning and took him to the 42nd Precinct for questioning before charging him with murder. The suspect has been charged with murder, the NYPD said. “The NYPD will be relentless in our efforts to get dangerous people out of our communities, especially when it involves the murder of a 15-year-old boy,” the department said on X Wednesday. Javits was shot in the stomach near Crotona Park on October 29, 2026. Police officers rushed him to St. Barnabas Hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The suspect’s identity has not been released because he is a minor. The NYPD says it is still searching for other people who may have been connected to the shooting. Javits’ father, Thomas Frimpong, said he was relieved that a suspect had been charged. Speaking emotionally at a press conference on Wednesday, he recalled that he was at work when he received news that his son had been shot. “I brought Javits from Ghana to continue his education here in the United States… He was very, very, very excited,” Thomas Frimpong said. “Unfortunately, on the 29th day of October, I was at work when I heard that my son had been shot.” Javits’ mother, Doris Gyamfi, travelled from Ghana to New York following the killing. She broke down in tears while addressing the press conference. “I need justice for my child,” Gyamfi said. “That’s all, I have only one child.” US civil rights lawyer Ben Crump, whose office released a statement on the case, said Javits had moved from Ghana to the United States about a year before his death. “We want these, apparently, kids who murdered Javits to be held fully accountable under the law, because that is equal justice,” Crump said. He said the teenager had dreams of becoming a doctor. The killing has sparked rallies and marches under the banner “Justice for Javits”, with hundreds of people attending a rally in the Bronx on Saturday to mourn the teenager and call for justice. New York City Public Schools said it would continue working with the NYPD as investigations proceed. DreamYard Preparatory School had not responded to ABC News’ request for comment at the time of its report. Javits moved from Ghana to the United States about a year before his death to join his father, Thomas Frimpong, who works as a yellow cab driver in New York. His father has previously said he believes the shooting may be connected to bullying his son experienced at school. That claim has not been established by investigators. The government, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, has been engaging with US authorities and the family. Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has said the government would cover the full cost of Doris Gyamfi’s travel to New York and contribute towards a dignified funeral for her son. Ghana’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations also engaged Ben Crump to assist in seeking justice for Ghanaians killed in the United States, at no cost to the Ghanaian taxpayer. The NYPD investigation remains ongoing, with detectives continuing efforts to identify and locate others who may have been involved in the shooting.

items.title: Marché financier : EDK mobilise 30 milliards de FCFA pour accélérer son expansion
items.description: Le Groupe EDK fait appel au marché financier régional pour mobiliser 30 milliards de FCFA à travers un emprunt obligataire ouvert à la souscription du 10 au 30 novembre 2026. Cette opération, rémunérée à 7,50 % sur sept ans, doit financer un vaste programme d’investissements, marqué notamment par l’ouverture de 45 nouveaux points de vente et le renforcement de ses capacités agro-industrielles. Le Groupe sénégalais EDK franchit un nouveau cap dans sa stratégie de développement. Créé en 2009, le groupe lance un emprunt obligataire par appel public à l’épargne de 30 milliards de FCFA, dénommé « EDK 7,50 % 2026-2033 ». Visée par l’AMF-UMOA sous le numéro EOP/26-05, l’opération porte sur trois millions d’obligations d’une valeur nominale de 10 000 FCFA chacune. Elle offre un taux d’intérêt annuel fixe de 7,50 %, sur une maturité de sept ans, avec deux années de différé de remboursement du capital. À travers cette levée de fonds, EDK entend financer une nouvelle phase de son expansion et consolider sa présence dans plusieurs secteurs de l’économie. Le programme d’investissement prévoit notamment l’ouverture de 45 nouveaux points de vente, répartis entre 15 stations-service EDK Oil, 15 magasins de grande distribution sous l’enseigne Low Price SA et 15 restaurants Djolof Chicken. L’enveloppe mobilisée contribuera également à la construction d’une nouvelle usine TEFESS Industrie, spécialisée dans la production d’aliments pour le bétail et la volaille. Le groupe prévoit, en outre, de moderniser les solutions de paiement de QuickPay, avec de nouveaux équipements, le développement du paiement sans contact et le renforcement de la sécurité des transactions. Cette nouvelle étape s’appuie sur une trajectoire de croissance déjà significative. En 2025, EDK a réalisé plus de 84 milliards de FCFA de chiffre d’affaires consolidé, avec un réseau de 111 points de vente et plus de 1 500 emplois directs et indirects. Le groupe avait notamment renforcé son activité de grande distribution en août 2025, avec la reprise de huit magasins précédemment exploités par CFAO Consumer, dont cinq Supeco et trois Carrefour Market. Pour son président-directeur général, Demba Ka, cette émission constitue un levier pour poursuivre la dynamique engagée depuis la création du groupe. « Les investissements que nous engageons aujourd’hui doivent nous permettre de poursuivre cette dynamique, d’étendre notre présence et de renforcer notre contribution à l’activité économique et à l’emploi », souligne-t-il. Structurée par Matha Securities, arrangeur et chef de file, avec CGF Bourse comme co-chef de file et MNS Capital comme conseiller financier, l’opération bénéficie d’une garantie couvrant 100 % du principal et des intérêts. Celle-ci est apportée par le Fonds de solidarité africain (FSA), à hauteur de 66,67 %, et le Fonds africain de garantie et de coopération économique (FAGACE), pour les 33,33 % restants. Oumar FEDIOR

items.title: Crisis looms in NDC as deputy national publicity secretary dumps party
items.description: By Henry Umoru Strong indications have emerged that crisis looms in the family of the opposition political party, the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC following the dumping of the party by the Deputy National Publicity Secretary, Hon. Abdulmumin Ohiare Abdulsalami. Abdulsalami announced his resignation on Wednesday night in a formal letter addressed to the National Chairman, NDC, Senator Moses Cleopas. He said he was “calling it quits and heading back home and avoiding orchestrated melodrama of exclusion from party affairs” He explained his decision in his letter titled: “Letter of resignation from the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC: withdrawal from all partisan commitments to the party” Abdulsalami said, “With a deep sense of gratitude to almighty Allah, I hereby notify the national and sub-national organs of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), through my former ward chairman, of my resignation from the party. I have also, by this notification, withdrawn from all ongoing technical and political commitments entered into at the pleasure of the National Leader of the NDC. “As a foundation member of the NDC, ditto a critical formative leader in the party, I am compelled to voluntarily take the exit having realized that my sincere and positive contributions to the meteoric rise and success of the party are at odds with the vested interests of a few powerful officers who call the shots. “More so, this painstaking decision serves my best interest as I prioritise my peace of mind rather than recurrent complaints at the sight of series of injustice meted out to me. “More so, I wish to sincerely appreciate the opportunity given to me by the National Leader of the NDC, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson to have served, firstly, as the Kogi State Protem Chairman, secondly, as the Deputy National Publicity Secretary/pioneer Spokesperson of the NDC, and, finally, as the Deputy National Director for Labour and Civil Society of the party. “And to my erstwhile colleague-friends, civil society activists and media practitioners with whom I have worked assiduously to promote the party, I cannot thank you enough for the comradeship and support you all have accorded me since the infancy of the party, and throughout my partisan stewardship thereupon.” In a related development, Dr. Yunusa Tanko has dumped the Presidential candidate of the NDC ahead of January 16 2027 election, Peter Obi as the national coordinator of the Obidient Movement for the North for the Social Democratic Party, SDP. He was announced the National Coordinator in September following a consensus to zone the position to the North. Obi appointed Tanko as national coordinator of the Obidient Movement in September 2024, following a consensus to zone the position to the North. Tanko previously served as Obi’s presidential campaign spokesman during the 2023 general elections, when the former Anambra State governor contested under the platform of the Labour Party (LP). He was also the presidential candidate of the Northern People’s Congress (NPC) in 2019 and became the party’s national chairman in 2023. The SDP on Wednesday inauagurated Yunusa Tanko as the national coordinator of its presidential campaign council for the 2027 general elections. Tanko’s appointment was announced during the inauguration of the party’s presidential campaign council in Abuja. The appointment was also confirmed by Mark Adebayo, Chief Media and Communications Adviser to the Adebayo/Bugaje Presidential Campaign Council. Speaking at the event, Tanko pledged to work with the SDP presidential candidate, Adewale Adebayo, and his running mate, Usman Bugaje, to secure victory in the 2027 elections. Describing the SDP as a left-wing, people-oriented political party, Tanko said it was committed to representing the interests of disadvantaged Nigerians who had been neglected by those in positions of authority. “The SDP is a left-wing political party. For those of you who do not know, we represent the interests of the downtrodden. The SDP represents those people that you neglect on the streets. So, that makes this particular party people-oriented,” he said. Tanko who disclosed that he resigned as political adviser (North) to Peter Obi, presidential candidate NDC on October 30, explained that his resignation followed his appointment to the leadership of the National Consultative Front (NCFront), following the death of Ghali Na’Abba, the organisation’s former co-chairman and former Speaker of the House of Representatives. Tanko said he had reached out to Obi and Seriake Dickson, national leader of the NDC, expressing appreciation for their support during his tenure as coordinator of the Obidient Movement. Tanko who pledged to work with the NCFront leadership and Adebayo, noting that his relationship with the SDP presidential candidate dated back to 2023 and that both shared a commitment to building a better Nigeria, said, “In advancing our political mission to a new Nigeria that works for all, I pledge to remain consistent and committed to our unwavering belief in good governance, justice, equity, national loyalty and dedication, and an unwavering commitment to moving Nigeria from where it is today to a better and more prosperous nation,” he said. items.title: Procès de l’assassinat du chef de de Solenzo : La prison à vie prononcée contre 12 personnes au terme de trois jours d’audience criminelle
items.description: La chambre criminelle du Tribunal de Grande Instance (TGI) de Dédougou a rendu son délibéré ce mercredi 11 novembre 2026 à Solenzo, au terme de trois jours d'audiences intenses consacrées au jugement de l'assassinat de Dibissan Coulibaly, chef de canton de Solenzo. Sur les vingt personnes qui comparaissaient dans la salle de réunion de la Sofitex, douze ont été reconnues coupables de participation à une manifestation illicite, de destructions volontaires aggravées et de meurtre, écopant de peines allant de 12 mois de prison ferme jusqu'à la réclusion criminelle à perpétuité. Assorti d'une réparation solidaire de 75 millions de FCFA au profit des ayants droit du défunt, ce verdict marque une étape majeure dans la quête de justice et le retour à l'apaisement dans la province des Banwa. C'est dans un climat d'une solennité particulière que s'est tenu le procès du meurtre du chef de canton de Solenzo, feu Dibissan Coulibaly. Délocalisée pour l'occasion dans la salle de réunion de la Sofitex à Solenzo, la chambre criminelle du Tribunal de Grande Instance (TGI) de Dédougou a siégé sans désemparer les 9, 10 et 11 novembre 2026. Face à la gravité des faits et à l'émoi suscité par la disparition de cette figure coutumière emblématique, un important dispositif des Forces de Défense et de Sécurité (FDS) a été déployé afin de garantir la protection des magistrats, des accusés et du public. Au terme des débats à la barre, le tribunal a tranché avec fermeté sur la responsabilité des protagonistes. Sur les vingt accusés poursuivis, douze individus ont été reconnus coupables des faits de participation à une manifestation illicite, de destructions volontaires aggravées de biens et de meurtre. Le collège de juges a prononcé à leur encontre des peines échelonnées entre 12 mois de prison ferme et la peine d’emprisonnement à vie, accompagnées d'une amende ferme de 600 000 francs CFA. Sur le plan civil, les personnes condamnées ont été soumises à une obligation solidaire : elles devront verser la somme de 75 000 000 de francs CFA aux ayants droit de feu Dibissan Coulibaly en réparation du préjudice subi. L'instruction à l'audience a également permis de faire le tri des responsabilités individuelles. Le tribunal a prononcé six relaxe pour infraction non constituée, blanchissant entièrement ces prévenus des soupçons qui pesaient sur eux. En outre, deux autres accusés ont été relaxés des chefs de poursuite liés à la participation à une manifestation illicite. Cette appréciation nuancée traduit la volonté du siège de fonder ses intimes convictions sur des preuves matérielles et juridiques irréfutables. Dans un communiqué officiel rendu public à l'issue du délibéré, le Procureur du Faso près le TGI de Dédougou, HEMA Lamoussa, a salué le bon déroulement des opérations judiciaires. Le représentant du ministère public a exprimé sa gratitude envers la hiérarchie judiciaire pour le déploiement des moyens matériels, ainsi qu'envers le Haut-Commissaire de la province des Banwa et le président de la délégation spéciale de la commune de Solenzo pour leur soutien logistique. Saluant l'action déterminante des FDS dans la sécurisation des audiences, le Procureur du Faso, Chevalier de l'Ordre du mérite, a conclu en remerciant chaleureusement les populations locales pour leur esprit civique et leur étroite collaboration, indispensables au succès de ce rendez-vous de justice. items.title: 2027 Budget: Why COP31 climate negotiations should matter to Ghana
items.description: Climate finance is no longer just an environmental funding issue. It is increasingly a fiscal, economic development, and national security concern, with direct implications for government expenditure, public debt, and Ghana’s long-term development prospects. The growing threat of extreme weather events, including the risks associated with El Niño, poses significant challenges to vulnerable economies such as Ghana. Flooding destroys public infrastructure, often requiring unplanned government expenditure on reconstruction and rehabilitation. Droughts and irregular rainfall patterns undermine agricultural productivity, threaten food supplies and increase pressure on household incomes. Ghana’s Financial Stability Review warns that flood-related losses could reach approximately US$200 million annually by 2050, while the IMF’s 2026 assessment also highlights risks to cocoa production and rain-fed cereal yields. These climate-related disruptions have far-reaching consequences for household incomes, export earnings, food security and government finances. As Ghana prepares its 2027 national budget, the availability of international climate finance could significantly influence how much the country can invest in flood protection, agricultural resilience, the energy transition, coastal protection and disaster preparedness without placing additional pressure on public debt. The central question, therefore, is whether Ghana’s national budget will adequately account for the growing cost of climate change and identify credible financing sources to meet that cost. At the ongoing UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, the African Group of Negotiators (AGN), chaired by Ghana’s Nana Dr. Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, is pushing for greater access to climate finance to enable vulnerable economies to implement their climate action plans. For Ghana, the stakes are particularly high. If developed countries reduce bilateral climate assistance or redirect development funding, countries such as Ghana could face increased competition for concessional financing. The government may consequently have to rely more heavily on domestic borrowing or commercial financing to fund critical climate-related infrastructure. One of Africa’s major interests at COP31 is whether the international community can translate its climate finance commitments into accessible, predictable and affordable funding for countries on the frontlines of climate change. Climate finance commitments under scrutiny Addressing a press conference on Africa’s position at COP31, AGN Chair Nana Dr. Antwi-Boasiako Amoah said developed countries had no excuse to renege on their climate finance commitments. He stressed the importance of advanced economies honouring their obligations under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) to provide climate finance, as agreed in previous negotiations. “We need to be very clear about this process; it’s about they asking what you are doing in your country to address climate change. The [developing] countries have their national plans and policies. The countries have done nothing wrong in those historical emissions. “It’s not that we don’t know that our countries must do something, but we are reminding them that they have an obligation that they have to honour… The excuses are that there is no money, but our understanding is that there is money, but there is no money for climate, because they can get money for military interventions overnight, they can get money for energy security overnight, why can’t they get money for climate? It’s because climate is not their priority,” he emphasized. The African Group has indicated that it will push for a tripling of adaptation finance and the replenishment of the Green Climate Fund (GCF), arguing that vulnerable countries need substantially greater resources to strengthen resilience and implement their climate commitments. Ghana’s President, John Dramani Mahama, has also been named the Green Climate Fund Replenishment Champion for the Fund’s third replenishment cycle. In this role, he is expected to help mobilise resources and build political support for replenishing the Fund to finance climate action in developing countries. For Ghana, this presents an opportunity to leverage its leadership role in the international climate finance conversation to advance its national development priorities. “As Ghanaians, it presents a very clear, clean opportunity for us to take advantage of climate financing to scale up development in Ghana,” said Seidu Issifu, the Minister of State in charge of Climate Change and Sustainability. He believes COP31 presents a different opportunity for Ghana, particularly in moving beyond commitments towards tangible implementation. “We’re saying that in this conference, we want to stop talking. We want to translate pledges into action, deliverable action that can drive sustainability, that can drive climate action for us, that can build resilience for our communities. So what are we looking for? We’re looking for scale-up climate funding to support our economic development,” he stated. Ghana’s $53.3 billion climate ambition Ghana has an estimated US$53.3 billion climate financing ambition over the next decade to implement its climate action plans. Mobilising these resources will require a credible financing framework that brings together international climate finance, domestic revenue, private sector investment and innovative financing mechanisms. The challenge is not simply identifying the resources required but establishing how these funds can be mobilised, accessed and deployed to deliver measurable development outcomes. For the government, the 2027 budget offers an opportunity to demonstrate how climate considerations are being integrated into national economic planning and public expenditure. Investments in climate-resilient infrastructure, sustainable agriculture, renewable energy, coastal protection and disaster preparedness should not be treated as isolated environmental interventions. They are essential investments in economic stability, livelihoods, food security and the country’s long-term fiscal sustainability. The climate negotiations in Antalya, therefore, have direct implications for decisions being made in Accra. As Ghana prepares its 2027 budget, the outcome of COP31 and subsequent climate finance negotiations should inform the country’s fiscal priorities, financing strategy and development planning. Ultimately, the test of climate diplomacy will not be the number of pledges announced at international conferences, but whether those commitments translate into accessible resources that help countries such as Ghana protect their economies, strengthen resilience and secure sustainable development.

items.title: Baltimore : un Sénégalais à la tête du Département de protection des consommateurs et des licences commerciales
items.description: Mamadou Samba vient de franchir une nouvelle étape dans son parcours professionnel aux États-Unis. Le 5 novembre 2026, ce jeune Sénégalais a prêté serment comme premier directeur exécutif du Département de protection des consommateurs et des licences commerciales (CPBL) de la ville de Baltimore, dans l’État du Maryland. Une nomination qui met en lumière le parcours d’un Sénégalais bien implanté dans les sphères de la gouvernance municipale américaine. C’est une nouvelle responsabilité pour Mamadou Samba dans l’administration publique américaine. Confirmé par le Conseil municipal de Baltimore, il prend les commandes du Département de protection des consommateurs et des licences commerciales (Consumer Protection and Business Licensing – CPBL), une nouvelle structure créée sous l’autorité du maire Brandon Scott. Cette nomination revêt un caractère particulier : Mamadou Samba est le premier responsable exécutif de cette agence municipale. Sa mission consiste donc à mettre en place cette institution, à définir son organisation et à lui donner les moyens de remplir ses différentes missions. Au cœur de ses attributions figurent la protection des consommateurs, la gestion des licences commerciales et l’application des réglementations municipales encadrant les activités économiques. Il s’agit ainsi de contribuer à l’amélioration des relations entre les consommateurs, les commerçants et l’administration municipale, tout en veillant au respect des règles qui encadrent le fonctionnement des entreprises dans la ville de Baltimore. Une expérience forgée à Washington Cette nouvelle responsabilité s’inscrit dans la continuité d’un parcours déjà marqué par une expérience significative au sein des institutions municipales américaines. Mamadou Samba a notamment occupé les fonctions de directeur exécutif du Bureau des affaires africaines auprès de la maire de Washington, D.C., Muriel Bowser. À ce poste, il a assuré pendant plusieurs années l’interface entre l’administration de la capitale fédérale américaine et les 53 ambassadeurs africains accrédités aux États-Unis. Une fonction stratégique qui lui a permis de développer une connaissance approfondie des relations institutionnelles, de la diplomatie municipale et des enjeux de coopération entre les collectivités territoriales. Son engagement en faveur du développement local dépasse également le cadre américain. En 2019, il a fondé l’Institut panafricain pour le développement municipal (PIMD), une organisation consacrée au renforcement des capacités des collectivités territoriales et à l’amélioration de la gouvernance locale en Afrique de l’Ouest. À travers cette initiative, Mamadou Samba s’intéresse particulièrement aux défis auxquels les administrations locales africaines sont confrontées, notamment en matière de gestion publique, de développement territorial et de renforcement des compétences institutionnelles. Un nouveau défi à Baltimore À Baltimore, le défi est désormais d’une autre dimension. En prenant la direction d’une agence entièrement nouvelle, il lui revient de construire les fondations administratives et opérationnelles d’un département appelé à jouer un rôle dans la régulation de la vie économique locale. La protection des consommateurs, l’encadrement des activités commerciales et la délivrance des autorisations nécessaires à l’exercice de certaines activités constituent autant de chantiers qui nécessitent une coordination entre les services municipaux, les opérateurs économiques et les citoyens. O. FEDIOR

items.title: Famed ship SS United States to be sunk off coast of Florida
items.description: A ship that was once the fastest in the world and is longer than the Titanic will be sunk off the coast of Florida and turned into the world’s largest artificial ocean reef. The SS United States spent nearly 30 years docked in Philadelphia before it was moved to Florida, where it will soon become a home for sea life and an underwater attraction for marine enthusiasts. Activists unsuccessfully fought for the historic liner – which crossed the Atlantic Ocean hundreds of times – to be preserved as a museum. Instead, after a Florida county purchased it, it will be added to the dozens of artificial reefs off the coast, and a land-based museum detailing the ship’s history is also planned. Before its retirement, the SS United States was known for carrying royalty and celebrities from the US to Europe, beginning in 1952 and ending in 1969. A young Bill Clinton, before he was president, used the ship to cross the Atlantic. Former presidents Harry Truman, Dwight Eisenhower and John Kennedy also travelled on the vessel. The ship moved from Philadelphia to Alabama last year for cleaning and remediation. On Monday, it took its final journey from Alabama to the coast of Destin, Florida, where it will be sunk on Wednesday in a precision operation without explosives. A 2015 image from when the ship was docked in Philadelphia Stars including Marlon Brando, Coco Chanel, Duke Ellington, Salvador Dali, Walt Disney, Judy Garland and Cary Grant also boarded the ship during its sailing lifetime. Before the municipal Florida government purchased it, several proposals to give the ship a second life as a museum or floating hotel failed. SS United States in the 1950’s Instead, the famed ship sat at various docks with various owners as legal battles played out. The SS United States Conservancy group repeatedly attempted to keep the ship above water, but was unsuccessful. Conservancy President Susan Gibbs – whose grandfather helped design the SS United States – said she was glad that the story of the ship would live on. “[The ship] has always been this unabashedly American symbol that brings so many people together,” Gibbs told CBS News, the BBC’s US partner.

items.title: Canada to fast-track permanent residence for 200,000 foreigners in 2027
items.description: The Canada government has announced plans to accelerate permanent residence (PR) processing for up to 200,000 foreign nationals already living in the country in 2027, as part of efforts to reduce immigration application backlogs and provide greater certainty for newcomers. The initiative, announced by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) under the 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, will provide additional admissions spaces for selected workers and humanitarian applicants seeking to transition to permanent residence. According to the government, the measure will be implemented through two major groups: a workers’ cohort and a humanitarian cohort, with up to 100,000 spaces allocated to each. The workers’ category will cover eligible foreign workers already living in Canada, alongside their accompanying family members. The government intends to work with provincial and territorial authorities to identify workers who meet regional labour market requirements. Eligible workers will include those who qualify for permanent residence through the Provincial Nominee Program (PNP), as well as applicants awaiting decisions under selected federal immigration programmes. These programmes include the Atlantic Immigration Program, Start-Up Visa Program, Self-Employed Persons Program, Agri-Food Pilot and Home Care Worker programmes. The humanitarian category, also allocated up to 100,000 spaces, will cover people already in Canada who have been waiting for permanent residence decisions, including applicants under specific family reunification and humanitarian pathways. Among those expected to benefit from the humanitarian allocation are: Spouses, common-law partners and dependent children: Family members of Canadian citizens and permanent residents who have already applied for permanent residence and are awaiting final decisions. Hong Kong residents: Applicants under Canada’s permanent residence pathways for Hong Kong residents, which closed to new applications on August 31, 2026. Ukrainian nationals: Applicants under the Ukraine Family Reunification Pathway, which closed to new applications on October 22, 2024. Humanitarian and compassionate applicants: Individuals already in Canada whose applications for permanent residence have received approval in principle. The government said the additional spaces would help it process all remaining applications under the Hong Kong and Ukraine pathways, while also supporting family reunification and fulfilling existing humanitarian commitments. IRCC also said the initiative would help reduce waiting periods for spouses and partners of Canadian citizens and permanent residents, with the aim of bringing processing times closer to 12 months for applicants destined for provinces outside Quebec. The department clarified that eligible applicants do not need to submit a separate application or take additional steps to be considered under the temporary initiative. However, the measure does not represent a new immigration pathway for people applying from outside Canada. It is specifically designed for individuals already living in the country who fall within the selected categories. The 200,000 additional spaces will also be separate from Canada’s regular permanent residence admissions target of 380,000 for 2027. Under its 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, Canada intends to maintain annual permanent residence admissions at 380,000, while targeting 370,000 new temporary resident arrivals, comprising 220,000 workers and 150,000 international students in 2027. The initiative forms part of Canada’s broader efforts to stabilise its immigration system, address labour shortages, reduce application backlogs and support people who have already established lives and communities in the country. items.title: There is a problem with Ghana’s school system – Prof Ayeetey
items.description: Professor of Development Economics at the Institute of Statistical, Social and Economic Research (ISSER) at the University of Ghana, Professor Ernest Ayeetey, says that Ghana’s school system is facing a serious quality problem, citing declining university progression rates among students of some of the country’s leading secondary schools. He said even established schools such as Achimota School were struggling to maintain the standards they were known for in the past. Speaking at the Achimota Speaks event on Wednesday, November 11, he said the chances of students progressing to university after attending Achimota School had declined significantly compared with previous years. “Today, if you go to Achimota School, your chances of not earning a beneficiary institution are more than 35 per cent. In some cases, in some years, more than 40 per cent,” he said. “In the good old days, if you went to Achimota School and you didn’t end up in university, you were part of some five per cent.” Prof Ayeetey explained that although some students might not gain university admission on their first attempt in the past, many eventually secured places after subsequent attempts. He said the situation was no longer the same, arguing that the decline was not limited to Achimota School but affected other leading secondary schools across the country. “So there’s enough evidence that there is a problem with the school system, and it’s not only Achimota School. All the best schools in Ghana have the same problem,” he said. Prof Ayeetey criticised what he described as the tendency for education policy changes to be driven by the personal preferences of individuals rather than broad consultations and evidence of public dissatisfaction. “Many of the changes that we’ve seen in education, and education has seen more changes than any other sector in this country. Many of the changes have been prompted by personal preferences,” he said. He cited instances where officials returned from international conferences impressed by education systems in other countries and subsequently pushed for similar changes in Ghana. “Individuals go to conferences, they sit by somebody from Malaysia, and the Malaysian tells them about how they are doing and is impressed. Now as soon as they return to Ghana, they start a memo to the minister, they start a memo to the chief director, and that’s how our changes are. They will push and push and push,” he said. He argued that many of the changes had not produced meaningful improvements in educational outcomes, despite the number of reforms introduced over the years.
