Upper West Region honours fallen heroes on 81st Remembrance Day
items.description: At the eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month, the usual morning bustle of Wa came to a sudden, solemn halt. A siren pierced the air, signalling two minutes of silence at the Upper West Regional Veterans Administration Ghana Cenotaph. It was a moment of profound reflection as the region marked the 81st Remembrance Day, honouring the men and women who sacrificed their lives in the World Wars and various global peacekeeping missions. The ceremony, steeped in history and reverence, was organised to remind the living of the heavy price paid for the freedoms enjoyed today. Retired Lieutenant Colonel Robert Zubaviel, a member of the Veterans Administration Ghana in the Upper West Region, highlighted the emotional and historical significance of the occasion. He noted that the annual gathering was an important observance commemorating the end of the global conflicts and paying tribute to those who laid down their lives to secure the peace enjoyed today. He emphasised that the ceremony was not only for soldiers who perished but also for civilians who lost their lives in the crossfire of the conflicts. The sentiment was reinforced when Zubaviel recited the traditional remembrance verse, which solemnly declares that the fallen heroes will not grow old as the living do, nor will the passing years condemn them to oblivion. The verse affirms the enduring promise that society will remember their sacrifices at sunset and in the morning. The ceremony was guided by Masters of Ceremony 2nd Lieutenant Denis Okumko and Lance Corporal Appah Kingsford, who led participants through the history of the armistice and the symbolic significance of the red poppy. The parade featured contingents from various regional security agencies, including the mechanised battalion, Police Service, Prisons Service, Fire Service and Immigration Service. The spiritual aspect of the event was led by military clergy, including Captain Sahmu-Deen Ridwan and Reverend Father Sub-Lieutenant Philip Yaw Nsobiaba, who offered prayers for the departed. Following the sounding of the Last Post and Reveille, the ceremony proceeded to one of its most solemn moments: the laying of wreaths. The wreath-laying ceremony served as a symbol of the region’s gratitude to the fallen heroes. Regional Minister Charles Lwanga Puozuing, representing the President, laid the first wreath on behalf of the government and people of Ghana. He was joined by regional security heads and traditional leaders. A representative of the Veterans Administration Ghana, retired Major Albert Donchebe, also laid a wreath in honour of his fallen comrades. A representative of the widows of veterans also laid a wreath, serving as a reminder of the enduring grief borne by military families.

items.title: Spain intercepts 2.6 tonnes of cocaine shipped from Tema Port
items.description: Spanish authorities have seized 2.6 tonnes of cocaine concealed in a shipment of coconuts from Ghana, the latest in a series of major overseas drug interceptions involving consignments traced to the country’s ports. Two men have been arrested in connection with the consignment after investigators tracked the cargo from the port of Valencia to a warehouse in Almería. The drugs were hidden in two containers of coconuts loaded at the Tema Port on August 2. The containers arrived in Valencia 20 days later, where customs officials and the Guardia Civil selected them for inspection after identifying them as presenting a high risk of drug trafficking. A search uncovered packages of cocaine concealed beneath false bottoms fitted into the wooden crates used to carry the coconuts. Tests confirmed that the white powder was cocaine. #OperacionesGC | ¡2.600 kilos de cocaína intervenidos en el Puerto de #Valencia! La droga viajaba oculta en dobles fondos de cajas de cocos procedentes de Ghana. 2 detenidos en Viator (#Almería) tras el seguimiento de la mercancía. Operación conjunta de la @guardiacivil y @aduanassva. — Guardia Civil (@guardiacivil) November 11, 2026 Investigators removed the drugs but left the containers sealed, allowing them to monitor the cargo and identify those who would eventually take delivery. Their surveillance led them to two refrigerated lorries that arrived to collect the containers. Officers followed the vehicles to a warehouse at the La Juaida industrial estate in Almería. The arrests were made as the cargo was being unloaded. Those detained were identified as the suspected importer of the drugs and the person responsible for supervising the unloading. Spanish authorities released details of the seizure on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. Another major seizure linked to Ghana The Spanish operation adds to a growing list of drug interceptions overseas involving shipments dispatched from Ghana. In September 2026, French customs seized nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine concealed in a container carrying plastic waste from Ghana at the port of Dunkirk. The consignment was valued at approximately €225 million, equivalent to about US$261 million. The seizure triggered investigations in Ghana, with the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) announcing the arrest of three suspects. Several other people were subsequently arrested and put before the courts over their alleged roles in the shipment. The case has drawn attention to the handling of export containers at the Tema Port, after investigations reportedly raised questions about abnormalities detected in scan images before the containers were cleared for shipment. In another case, a Syrian national was arrested at Beirut’s Rafic Hariri International Airport on October 31, 2026, after arriving from Accra with about 40 kilogrammes of suspected cocaine concealed in two pieces of luggage. NACOC confirmed the arrest and said it was working with Lebanese authorities to identify and apprehend alleged accomplices in Ghana. The seizures follow major interceptions in Europe in 2025. In November that year, Belgian authorities found 2,829 kilogrammes of cocaine concealed in cassava flour shipped from Tema to Antwerp. A further 1,158 kilogrammes of suspected cocaine from Ghana was intercepted at the same port in December. Earlier, in June 2025, Dutch customs seized 4.5 tonnes of cocaine hidden in a timber consignment from Tema at the Port of Amsterdam. The seizure was reported as the largest in the port’s history at the time. The problem has also extended beyond cocaine. In June 2026, Australian authorities announced the seizure of 320 kilogrammes of methamphetamine concealed in a charcoal shipment from Ghana. Ghana’s growing international exposure The series of interceptions has raised concerns about the use of Ghanaian ports and legitimate export cargo by international drug trafficking networks. Figures from Belgian customs, reported by JoyNews Research in September 2026, placed Ghana as the fifth-largest country of origin for cocaine seized at the port of Antwerp in 2025. Ghana was the only African country among the five leading countries on the list. The classification refers to the country from which the cargo was shipped, rather than where the cocaine was produced. The report noted that the drugs were believed to originate from South America and were concealed in legitimate exports. Again, a JoyNews tally, published in September, counted 28 narcotics-related cases linked to Ghana since January 2025, including 11 involving cocaine. The cocaine seizures with published weights amounted to approximately 15.8 tonnes. The September seizure in France also prompted President John Dramani Mahama to convene a meeting of security chiefs and direct an inter-agency task force to review the country’s systems for detecting narcotics at ports and borders. The recurring interceptions have brought renewed scrutiny to cargo inspection, intelligence-sharing and cooperation among agencies responsible for securing Ghana’s ports and international supply chains.

items.title: Manchester United : accord de principe avec Mauricio Pochettino
items.description: Manchester United a franchi une étape importante dans sa quête d’un nouvel entraîneur. Selon Fabrizio Romano et plusieurs médias britanniques, le club mancunien a trouvé un accord verbal de principe avec Mauricio Pochettino pour qu’il devienne son prochain entraîneur. Les discussions doivent désormais se poursuivre avec la Fédération américaine de football, auprès de laquelle Pochettino est encore sous contrat. Une clause libératoire d’environ 10 millions de dollars permettrait à Manchester United de s’attacher ses services. L’arrivée de l’entraîneur argentin reste toutefois liée à la décision finale concernant Michael Carrick. Le technicien anglais est toujours en poste et a dirigé l’entraînement de Manchester United mercredi, mais les dirigeants du club doivent se réunir pour statuer sur son avenir. Pochettino, actuellement sélectionneur des États-Unis, serait désormais prêt à rejoindre les Red Devils. Il est considéré comme le favori pour succéder à Carrick, alors que Manchester United connaît un début de saison particulièrement compliqué et pointe dans la zone de relégation en Premier League. L’ancien entraîneur de Tottenham et de Chelsea a déjà été approché à plusieurs reprises par Manchester United par le passé. Cette fois, les négociations semblent avoir franchi un cap décisif. items.title: US withdraws from U17 World Cup in Qatar over security fears
items.description: The United States has withdrawn from the upcoming Under-17 soccer World Cup in Qatar due to concerns about security in the Middle East, US media reported Wednesday. Players were informed of the decision just over a week before the tournament is due to begin on November 19, US Soccer Collective and The Athletic reported, citing anonymous sources. US Soccer, the sport’s governing body in the United States, did not immediately confirm the news or respond to AFP’s request for comment. The war in the Middle East began in February with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which retaliated by targeting, among others, Gulf countries allied with Washington. Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have been punctuated by repeated threats from the United States and Israel to resume bombardments of Iran. Multiple sporting events in the Middle East have been affected, including the tennis WTA Finals which were scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia — which neighbors Qatar — but are instead now taking place at Indian Wells in the US. This season’s Formula One Grand Prix in Jeddah was cancelled, while the race in Bahrain was called off and later rescheduled under the same name in Malaysia. Several events in Saudi Arabia have also been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following attacks on the country by the Houthis in Yemen. The US is one of 48 teams scheduled to play in the Under-17 World Cup, in a group with Montenegro, Chile and Algeria. The Under-17 World Cup shifted to an annual event last year, and is being held in Qatar for five consecutive years. Announcing its host decision in 2024, FIFA said the decision to choose a single host nation for multiple editions centered on the ability to make “use of existing footballing infrastructure in the interest of tournament efficiencies and sustainability”. Qatar was the venue for the 2022 men’s World Cup. Vanguard News The post US withdraws from U17 World Cup in Qatar over security fears appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: WASEC 1984 year group donates 80 tables and 160 benches worth GH¢96,000 to alma mater
items.description: The 1984 year group of Wa Senior High School (WASEC) has donated dining hall furniture worth GH¢96,000 to the school. The donation, comprising 80 tables and 160 benches made of plywood and metal, was officially handed over to the school on Wednesday as part of the Students’ Representative Council (SRC) Week celebrations. The Headmaster of the school, Iddrisu Adams Thirdman, who received the items, described this year’s celebration as unique. He said the furniture would go a long way towards easing pressure on the school’s dining hall. The Wa Municipal Chairman of the Wa Secondary School Old Students Association (WASOSA), Dr Solomon Dansie, said the school’s dining hall was built in the 1980s to serve about 700 students but currently caters for more than 2,000 students, with only 25 tables and benches. He said he raised the challenge on the WASOSA national platform, where it was taken up by a member of the 1984 Year Group based in the United States, Seydu Mahama Sumani. Speaking on behalf of the group, alumni representative Laweh Emmanuel said Mr Sumani led the group and spearheaded the project to its successful completion under the leadership of the group’s Chairman, Alhaji Mohamed Ahmed. Mr Laweh said the school had shaped their lives through discipline, resilience, love and lifelong friendship, making it their responsibility to give back. Dr Dansie noted that almost all members of the 1984 Year Group were retirees and described their contribution as a major sacrifice. The Headmaster also used the occasion to appeal to the Speaker of Parliament, Alban Bagbin, who is constructing a 2,000-capacity auditorium for the school, to consider the need for a bigger facility. He said the student population was less than 2,000 when the project began but had since grown to nearly 3,000, adding that the school would soon need a bigger auditorium. The 1984 Year Group urged current students to take good care of the furniture and, in turn, give back to the school when they complete their education.

items.title: Alerte météo : pluies ou averses localement fortes avec risque de grêle et fortes rafales de vent, mercredi et jeudi
items.description: La Direction générale de la météorologie (DGM), a annoncé des pluies ou averses localement fortes avec risque de grêle et de fortes rafales de vent avec chasse-poussières locales attendues, mercredi et jeudi, dans plusieurs provinces du Royaume. Dans un bulletin d'alerte météorologique actualisé de niveau de vigilance orange, la DGM précise que ces précipitations, oscillant entre 80 et 110 mm, sont prévues de mercredi à 18h00 à jeudi à 12h00, dans les provinces de Chefchaouen, Al Hoceima, Tétouan, Essaouira, Chichaoua, Agadir-Ida-Ou-Tanane, Inezgane-Ait Melloul et Chtouka-Ait Baha. Ce même phénomène (40 à 80 mm) est également prévu, durant la même période, dans les provinces de Taounate, Larache, Sidi Kacem, Kénitra, Taza, Ouezzane, Tiznit et Taroudant. Ces pluies ou averses, avec des cumuls de 20 à 40 mm, devraient également toucher les provinces de Fahs-Anjra, Tanger-Assilah, M'diq-Fnideq, Driouch, Sefrou, Fès, Moulay Yacoub, Meknès, El Hajeb, Ifrane, Khémisset, Sidi Slimane, Salé, Rabat, Skhirate-Témara, Mohammedia, Casablanca, Benslimane, Nouaceur, Médiouna, Berrechid, El Jadida, Settat, Sidi Bennour, Khouribga, Fquih Ben Salah, Béni Mellal, Khénifra, Azilal, Safi, Youssoufia, Rehamna, El Kelaâ des Sraghna, Marrakech, Al Haouz, Sidi Ifni, Guelmim, Tan-Tan et Tarfaya. Par ailleurs, de fortes rafales de vent (90 à 100 km/h) avec chasse-poussières locales sont attendues, mercredi de 18h00 à 23h00, dans les provinces de Sidi Bennour, Safi, Chichaoua, Essaouira, Youssoufia, Tétouan, El Jadida, Al Haouz, Taza, Driouch, Al Hoceima, Tanger-Assilah et Chefchaouen. Le même phénomène (80 à 90 km/h) est prévu, durant la même période, dans les provinces de Rehamna, Settat, El Kelaâ des Sraghna, Khouribga, Rabat, Berrechid, Benslimane, Guercif, Errachidia, Témara-Skhirate, Salé, Nouaceur, Mohammedia, Médiouna, Casablanca, Kénitra, Marrakech, M'diq-Fnideq, Larache, Fahs-Anjra, Sefrou, Ifrane, El Hajeb, Figuig et Khémisset. items.title: Décolonisation : quand Cuba épaulait les combattants africains
items.description: À travers son ouvrage « Cuba et la guerre d’indépendance de la Guinée-Bissau et du Cap-Vert : la chute du dernier empire colonial en Afrique », l'ancien combattant cubain Víctor Dreke revient sur l'engagement de son pays aux côtés des mouvements de libération africains. Une contribution historique que l'historien Amadou Ba juge importante pour éclairer un épisode encore méconnu de la décolonisation du continent. L'histoire des indépendances africaines ne s'est pas écrite uniquement sur le continent. Elle s'est également nourrie de solidarités internationales, de collaborations militaires et d'engagements politiques venus d'ailleurs. L'intervention cubaine dans la guerre de libération de la Guinée-Bissau et du Cap-Vert en constitue une illustration. C'est cet épisode que remet en lumière Víctor Dreke dans son livre intitulé « Cuba et la guerre d’indépendance de la Guinée-Bissau et du Cap-Vert : la chute du dernier empire colonial en Afrique ». Dans cet ouvrage, l'ancien combattant de la révolution cubaine livre un témoignage sur la participation de son pays à la lutte menée contre la domination portugaise. À travers son expérience, il revient sur les conditions de vie des combattants, les stratégies militaires, les relations avec les cadres africains ainsi que les difficultés rencontrées sur le terrain. Dans son regard critique sur le livre, le Dr Amadou Ba, historien, auteur et professeur d'histoire à l'Université Laurentienne, souligne l'intérêt documentaire et historique de cette publication. Il y voit une contribution importante à une histoire encore insuffisamment connue : celle de l'engagement cubain dans les luttes de libération africaines. Plus de 400 Cubains ont participé à cette mission entre 1966 et 1974. Leur intervention ne s'est toutefois pas limitée à l'accompagnement militaire. Elle associait également assistance médicale, formation et soutien logistique aux combattants du Parti africain pour l'indépendance de la Guinée et du Cap-Vert (PAIGC). Des médecins cubains ont notamment pris part aux soins des combattants et des populations vivant dans les zones libérées. Une solidarité sans substitution L'un des enseignements majeurs de cet ouvrage réside dans la place accordée au leadership africain. L'historien Amadou Ba insiste sur le fait que le récit ne présente pas les Cubains comme les libérateurs de la Guinée-Bissau. Il restitue plutôt à Amílcar Cabral et au PAIGC leur rôle central dans la conduite de la lutte. L'aide cubaine s'inscrivait, en effet, dans une dynamique internationale plus large. L'Union soviétique, la Chine, la Tchécoslovaquie, la Guinée-Conakry, l'Algérie, l'Égypte, la Yougoslavie et la Suède avaient également apporté différents types de soutien au mouvement de libération. Les volontaires cubains se distinguaient néanmoins par leur participation directe aux combats aux côtés des forces guinéennes. Au-delà de la dimension militaire, le livre met en exergue la pensée politique d'Amílcar Cabral. Pour le dirigeant du PAIGC, la victoire armée ne constituait pas une fin en soi. Elle devait ouvrir la voie à une transformation profonde des conditions de vie des populations. L'organisation des zones libérées, avec la création d'écoles, de cliniques, de structures sanitaires et d'administrations villageoises, traduisait cette ambition. Une victoire aux répercussions internationales L'ouvrage replace également la guerre de Guinée-Bissau dans le contexte de l'effondrement de l’empire colonial portugais. L'enlisement des forces portugaises dans les guerres africaines a contribué à la crise du régime de Lisbonne, jusqu'au coup d'État militaire du 25 avril 1974, qui ouvre la voie à la Révolution des œillets. Après la proclamation unilatérale de l'indépendance de la Guinée-Bissau en septembre 1973, le Portugal finit par la reconnaître en septembre 1974. Le Cap-Vert accède à son tour à la souveraineté en juillet 1975. Pour Amadou Ba, cette dimension transnationale constitue l'un des apports majeurs du livre. Les luttes africaines ont ainsi participé à des bouleversements politiques bien au-delà du continent. L'historien relève toutefois certaines limites au témoignage de Víctor Dreke. Écrit plusieurs décennies après les événements par un acteur profondément attaché à la révolution cubaine, le récit valorise naturellement l'internationalisme et la solidarité entre les peuples. Certaines questions, notamment les tensions internes au PAIGC, les perceptions locales de la présence cubaine ou encore les débats au sein du gouvernement cubain, auraient mérité un examen plus approfondi. Ces réserves ne diminuent cependant pas l'intérêt historique de l'ouvrage. Pour Amadou Ba, il constitue à la fois un témoignage de première main, un document de mémoire révolutionnaire et une ressource pour mieux comprendre les dynamiques de la décolonisation africaine. En donnant à voir les liens tissés entre Bissau, Conakry, La Havane et Lisbonne, Víctor Dreke rappelle finalement que les indépendances africaines ont aussi été le produit de solidarités qui ont traversé les frontières et les océans. A.N

items.title: Why Dr. Farouk Aliu Mahama remains NPP’s best bet to reclaim Yendi seat in 2028
items.description: In politics, numbers do not lie. And the numbers from Yendi in the 2020 and 2024 elections tell a very clear story. From the numbers, it’s clear Dr. Farouk Aliu Mahama did not lose Yendi in 2024 because the people rejected him; he lost because the NPP was divided, and because a national wave of apathy hit the party everywhere. If the NPP wants to win back Yendi in 2028 and maximise votes for Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, there is only one politically wise decision: rally behind Farouk Aliu Mahama. Here are seven reasons: 1. 2024 was not a rejection ; it was a split Let us look at the facts. In the 2020 Yendi parliamentary election, Farouk Aliu Mahama, contesting for the first time, polled 40,624 to win by a whopping 62.14 per cent. His main opponent, the NDC’s Alhassan Abdul Fatawu, polled 24,755, representing 37.86 per cent. From the data, Farouk won by a massive 15,869 votes – one of the biggest winning margins in the entire Northern Region by the NPP. Then in the 2024 Yendi Parliamentary election, Alhassan Abdul Fatawu polled 30,770 to win the seat against Farouk Aliu Mahama, who polled 30,441 and NPP-affiliated Independent Candidate, Hussein Abdul-Karim, who polled 4,324. From the data above, Farouk lost narrowly by just 329 votes. That is the whole story. Farouk did not collapse. He was split. The independent candidate, who came from within the NPP family after the bitter and disputed primaries, took 4,324 votes – votes that in 2020 would have gone to the NPP. If the NPP had gone into 2024 united, Farouk would have, despite the widespread national apathy against the NPP, won with over 34,000 votes against the NDC’s 30,770. Even in division, even in crisis, even when his own party members campaigned against him, Farouk still almost won. That is not weakness, but a proof that he is firm on the ground. In many NPP strongholds across the country, many MPs lost by 5,000, 10,000, 15,000 votes in 2024. But Farouk, battling serious internal division, lost by 329. In a year of disaster for the NPP, he held the line. 2. Apathy affected everyone, not just Farouk The second factor was widespread national apathy that hit the NPP in 2024 also hit Yendi too. The NPP’s parliamentary votes in Yendi dropped from 40,624 in 2020 to 30,441 in 2024, just as in all constituencies across the country including the party’s stronghold. The NPP’s presidential votes also dropped sharply, despite Dr. Bawumia winning the constituency. There are two lessons from this: First, the drop was not personal to Farouk, nor was it to Dr. Bawumia. It was a party-wide problem across the country due to reluctance by party members to go out and vote, as the NPP’s own Mike Oquaye report found. When apathy hits, every candidate suffers and Farouk was not an exception. Second, and most important, is that even in that difficult year, the NDC candidate who won Yendi did not win a significant share of the votes that dropped from Farouk’s 2020 numbers; neither did President John Mahama. The NDC moved from 24,755 in 2020 to 30,770 in 2024 – an increase of about 6,000 votes. Farouk lost about 10,000 votes from his 2020 total. Where did the rest go? They did not go to the NDC. They went to apathy and to the independent candidate. That means the people of Yendi did not switch to the NDC. They stayed home, or they voted for the independent out of internal NPP anger. Those voters are recoverable. They are NPP voters, and the man who can bring them back is undoubtedly Farouk. 3. Maximising Presidential votes Note this carefully: In 2024, while Farouk narrowly lost the parliamentary race, Dr. Bawumia still won the presidential race in Yendi with 32,239 against Mahama’s 31,664. How did Bawumia win Yendi when the NPP parliamentary candidate lost? Because Farouk’s structures, his campaign, and his groundwork kept the NPP competitive in Yendi even in a divided house. He was able to complement Bawumia’s campaign through the NPP’s great record of development in the area. If Farouk is on the ballot as a united NPP candidate in 2028, he will not only win back the seat; he will maximise votes for Dr. Bawumia. A united Yendi means a bigger presidential margin. A divided Yendi means the party will fight itself instead of fighting the NDC. 4. A record the people cannot forget Beyond the numbers, there is Farouk’s remarkable record from the only time he has been MP. And in Yendi, the record is visible and verifiable. In his first term as MP, Farouk Aliu Mahama delivered an impressive record of development and community support: Roads were built and reshaped. Schools were renovated and new ones built. Farmers were supported with farm inputs and equipment. The youth received skills training and business support. Communities received water, health support, and educational assistance. The beautification of Yendi township is a clear, visible example that everyone can see. It is not a promise on a poster; it is on the ground. The people of Yendi are attesting to it themselves. They saw development, they felt it and they lived it. 5. He did not abandon the people after losing Many politicians disappear after losing an election, only to resurface four years later to ask for votes again. But Farouk did the opposite. After losing in 2024, he did not abandon Yendi. He continued to show commitment to the progress of Yendi and its people. He continued to support community projects and individuals, especially in job-seeking and education. He stayed with the people in defeat as he did in victory. That is character! That is leadership! And the people have noticed. 6. The comparison is already being made Today, the people of Yendi are comparing Farouk’s high standard with the incumbent, who is struggling to replicate it. The incumbent has not matched the expectations. The projects have slowed, the energy has dropped and the presence has reduced. When the people themselves are calling for the one who once made things possible for them, a strategic party listens. The electorate cannot forget a man who changed their community, supported their children, and stood with them. When they exchanged Farouk for someone else, they expected more but they got less. That is why the call for his return is growing louder every day. 7. The NPP must not deepen old cracks This is the political lesson for the NPP in Yendi: Do not reinvent the wheel to deepen old cracks and open new ones. The 2024 defeat was caused by division and the solution cannot be more division. The solution cannot be to bring a new, untested candidate who will reopen old wounds, create new factions, and start from zero. The solution is unity! The NPP must demonstrate unity and rally behind the young and dynamic Farouk Aliu Mahama, who has proven that he is firm on the ground even when faced with crisis. He has the structures. He has the youth. He has the women. He has the chiefs and opinion leaders. He has the track record. He has the love of the people. Why throw that away? Conclusion: Act politically right Politics is about winning. And winning requires choosing the candidate who can win. Farouk Aliu Mahama lost in 2024 by 329 votes while fighting his own party and the bigger “enemy”. Imagine what he will do in 2028 with a united party behind him. The NPP in Yendi does not need an experiment; it needs a proven winner. It needs a man who has delivered, who has stayed, and who the people themselves are asking for. The party must repose massive confidence in the young man and unite behind him. And Yendi will return to the NPP, with Dr. Bawumia getting the votes he deserves from Yendi. The people have spoken through their calls. Now the party must act.

2027 Budget should protect fiscal credibility, direct scarce public resources towards productive capacity – KPMG Boss
items.description: The Country Managing Partner of KPMG, Andy Akoto, wants the 2027 Budget to protect fiscal credibility while directing scarce public and private resources towards productive capacity, jobs and infrastructure that can be implemented and maintained. Highlighting his expectations of the 2027 Budget, Mr. Akoto said Ghana enters the 2027 budget cycle from a stronger macroeconomic position, with growth remaining firm and inflation materially lower. “It is encouraging that the government continues to maintain economic stability. Real GDP [Gross Domestic Product] grew by 6.2% in the first half of 2026, with full-year growth projected at 5.7%, while inflation stood at 5.5% in October. The staff-level agreement on the first review under the IMF’s Policy Coordination Instrument provides a further basis for policy continuity. Reserve rebuilding, domestic revenue mobilisation and reform remain important to sustaining these gains”, he explained. According to him, businesses still have to manage credit risk, utility reliability, tax administration, working-capital pressures and uneven purchasing power. Against this background, KPMG and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) undertook the 2027 Pre-Budget Survey to assess business conditions and obtain views on priorities for the national budget. Our survey and focus group study bring together businesses’ perspectives on measures that can support investment, employment, and improved livelihoods. The report also considers how these priorities relate to Ghana’s development objectives and the practical requirements for implementation. About 70% of respondents expressed confidence in their organisation’s growth in 2027. However, less than half indicated improved operating-cost conditions. “Our focus group study also highlighted continued pressure from electricity, rent and limited purchasing power. Some businesses have benefited from more favourable conditions, while others continue to face difficulties in selling their products and financing day-to-day operations”, Mr. Akoto stated. According to him, the budget should therefore support productive activity and improve the conditions under which firms invest and reach customers. He also said access to affordable finance remains a prominent priority, stating that respondents called for low-interest loans and credit guarantees, whilst its focus group study identified collateral requirements, short repayment period, loan processing charges and limited awareness of support programmes as practical barriers to obtaining and using finance. As Ghana prepares the 2027 Budget, Mr. Akoto also pointed out that the proposed US$10 billion New Economy programme offers an opportunity to convert stability into productive transformation. “Its implementation should be coordinated with Big Push and other initiatives through a transparent, proritised investment pipeline. The Budget should clarify additional revenue requirements, financing sources and overlapping commitments, while leveraging shared infrastructure and sequencing complementary projects”, he alluded. He concluded that KPMG remains committed to contributing its expertise to help the government and businesses translate these priorities into sustainable practical outcomes.

items.title: The politics of reconciliation: A case for Lawyer Kwasi Kwarteng
items.description: As the NPP embarks on the difficult but necessary task of rebuilding party unity, it has an opportunity to demonstrate that unity is not merely a political slogan, but a commitment reflected in deliberate choices, difficult compromises and tangible acts of goodwill. Kwasi Kwarteng, who served as spokesperson for Hon. Kennedy Agyapong during one of the party’s fiercest flagbearership contests, distinguished himself by placing the interests of the NPP above personal allegiance. He promptly embraced Dr. Bawumia’s leadership and has since consistently worked across factional lines to promote reconciliation, even at a time when the party faced the real threat of fragmentation. His subsequent decision not to extend the internal rivalry into the National Communications Director contest, together with his sustained efforts in working for the party, demonstrates a willingness to subordinate personal ambition to the larger interests of the party. It would therefore send a powerful and reassuring message if Dr. Bawumia, the National Executive and the party leadership were to recognise and protect this investment in reconciliation by supporting a consensus arrangement that allows Kwasi Kwarteng to go unopposed in the Asante Akyem North parliamentary primaries. Such a gesture would go beyond the political interests of one individual or constituency. It would reassure disgruntled party members that reconciliation is genuine, demonstrate that loyalty and sacrifices are recognised, and give everyone a renewed sense of belonging in the NPP. It would also be a tangible demonstration to party faithfuls and the Ghanaian public that the NPP has genuinely turned the page, values those who build bridges and are prepared to make practical sacrifices in pursuit of a united political front.

items.title: About 32% of businesses to consider investing or expanding under 24-Hour Programme – KPMG UNDP Report
items.description: About 32% of businesses would consider investing or expanding under the 24-Hour Programme, a KPMG United Nations Development Programme survey has disclosed. Also, 44% of respondents would do so subject to suitable incentives or enabling conditions, while 14% needed more information and 10% would not participate. The factors that would encourage businesses to participate or invest in the 24-hour economy were access to finance, reliable and affordable utilities and tax incentives. The survey results demonstrated that business optimism remains constrained by the availability of finance, dependable utilities, market demand and the practical conditions required to invest. Respondents expressed conditional interest in the 24H+ programme and prioritised jobs and youth employment, while the focus group study highlighted documentation, customer access and cash-flow challenges. They therefore want government support to focus on usable finance, investable projects and implementation that produces sustained activity and employment. Move from loan availability to usable finance The survey revealed that interest rates, collateral and documentation remain material concerns even though some respondents reported improved borrowing conditions. Africa requires over US$1.3 trillion annually to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), according to AfDB, emphasising the importance of both mobilising finance and using it effectively. The Ghana Government has therefore been urged to set out a coordinated approach to attract additional capital through participating financial institutions and existing support networks, expanding products that match business cash flows. Again, credit guarantees need transparent eligibility, meaningful lender risk retention, prudent exposure limits and independent monitoring. Improve enterprise readiness and responsible access The report also wants the government to connect training with actual lender requirements and provide practical support for applications, financial statements and business plans. Among others, GIZ’s Invest for Jobs approach combines tailored advice, equipment support and investment readiness, illustrating the value of capability alongside capital. Seventy-five percent of the businesses surveyed were male, while 66.1% resided in the Greater Accra region.

items.title: Missing 11-month-old baby found buried alive in a crate in South Carolina
items.description: An 11-month-old baby has been rescued in South Carolina after officials say he was buried alive in a crate by his father. Koah Sharpe had been missing since Monday when he was taken by his father, Michael Comer, 25, according to the Lexington County Sheriff’s Department. Comer was arrested on a burglary charge on Monday evening but his son was not with him. The baby was found on Tuesday “buried alive” and “clinging to life” not far from his father’s house, Lexington County Sheriff Jay Koon said at a news conference. It is thought he had been there for 24 hours. The child is now in hospital receiving care, Koon said, adding he was hopeful he would make a full recovery. Police are still deciding what further charges to bring against the father. The search for baby Koah began on Monday after his father took him from his mother’s house. Comer’s mother was watching the child and had left her son alone with him briefly, Koon said, when he left abruptly with Koah. Officials allege the baby’s father buried him alive in a dog crate Comer was seen travelling to multiple locations without the baby and was later arrested in Lexington County without Koah. A search party of 100 police and fire department officials were then sent to search for the child, the sheriff said. He added that when they asked Comer where his son was, he “did not have much to say” about his whereabouts. Koon said that rescuers searched the woods near Comer’s house and saw some “freshly disturbed dirt”. As they began to dig, they heard a baby crying – something the sheriff described as “the most joyful sound you ever heard”. “The race was on. Everybody was getting down there trying to get him out,” Koon added. He said the crate was wrapped in a towel that probably provided enough air for Koah to survive for as long as he did, while the cold weather kept him from getting too hot. “The crate was, probably, I’m guessing about a two-foot [61cm] by two-foot dog crate. So, I think, once that crate hit the ground, he was probably up at least a foot from the top of that crate to the top of the ground,” Koon explained. Of the parents’ relationship, the sheriff said there were “obviously some issues”. Comer had previously pleaded guilty to domestic violence charges, court records show. Comer’s mother, Patricia Comer, told NBC News that Koah’s mother had full custody of him but allowed her to supervise while her son watched him. She said her son had watched the baby before unsupervised without any problems. “Honestly, I’m his mother, and I never expected this from him,” Patricia Comer said.

items.title: Only 36% of businesses described electricity as very or mostly reliable – KPMG, UNDP survey
items.description: A survey by professional services firm KPMG and the United Nations Development Programme has revealed that only 36% of businesses described electricity as very or mostly reliable. Forty-seven percent also experienced occasional interruptions and 44% prioritised affordable and predictable tariffs. The survey highlights the combined effect of power interruptions, affordability and billing. The report stated that the government and sector institutions should prioritise feeder-level reliability, meter accuracy, complaint resolution and the disclosure of service-quality performance in productive areas. “A tariff hold can provide stability but cannot substitute for operational improvement. ECG distribution reform should address billing accuracy, technical and commercial losses and a transparent treatment of public-service obligations”, the report stated. It pointed out that the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF’s) November review also highlighted the importance of completing the delayed audit of Electricity Company of Ghana collection accounts, adding any extended-hours tariff arrangement must be evaluated against cost recovery and actual electricity demand. The focus-group participants identified billing disputes and power interruptions as operational constraints affecting production and cash-flow planning. They therefore want better metering, distribution performance and transparent service standards, describing them as essential for reliable production. Seventy-five percent of the respondents surveyed were male, while 66.1% reside in the Greater Accra region.

items.description: Une panne survenue mercredi 11 novembre à 16h48 sur des lignes à très haute tension du réseau national de transport d’électricité a provoqué des interruptions de courant dans plusieurs quartiers de Casablanca et certaines zones de la province de Nouaceur. La société régionale multiservice (SRM) de Casablanca-Settat a expliqué que les coupures ont été provoquées par un incident sur le réseau national de transport d’électricité. Une défaillance est survenue sur des lignes à très haute tension (HTB) relevant de l’Office national de l’électricité et de l’eau potable (ONEE), précise la SRM dans un communiqué, notant que cet incident est lié aux fortes rafales de vent et aux orages qui ont touché la région, et a entraîné une interruption de l’alimentation de plusieurs postes de transformation desservant différents secteurs de la métropole. Les perturbations ont notamment concerné le centre-ville, Maârif, El Fida, Aïn Chock, Ben M'Sick, Sbata, Sidi Othmane et Hay Hassani. Dans la province de Nouaceur, Bouskoura, Oulad Azzouz et Dar Bouazza ont également été touchées. Dès la survenue de la panne, la SRM affirme avoir mobilisé ses équipes, en coordination avec l’ONEE, afin de procéder aux interventions nécessaires. Des manœuvres sur son réseau moyenne tension ont également été engagées pour limiter les répercussions de l’incident. Tout en s'excusant auprès clients concernés, la SRM a assuré que ses équipes restent mobilisées, avec l’ONEE, pour rétablir l’alimentation électrique dans les meilleurs délais. The post SRM Casablanca : les coupures d'électricité provoquées par une défaillance sur des HTB de l'ONEE appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: African writing award probe finds ‘no evidence’ winning story was AI generated
items.description: The Caine Prize for African Writing has said that after an internal review it has found no evidence that Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza had used generative AI to write his winning short story and confirmed him as the winner of this year’s £10,000 ($13,000) award. Ellah Wakatama, chair of the Caine Prize’s board of trustees, said the matter had been investigated following an article in US magazine The Atlantic with the headline, Yet Another Literary Prizewinner Seems to Be AI. “From our detailed investigation, we feel the evidence is clear: The Blue Fighter was human written,” she said in a video posted on X. The accusation had caused a social media uproar and Kundizeza had denied the allegation. The Atlantic article by journalist Vauhini Vara alleged that AI-detection software Pangram had shown his work about a boy whose family falls on hard times was entirely AI generated. Her allegations followed rows over other literary prizes this year, in particular the Commonwealth Short Story Prize, which was won by Trinidadian writer Jamir Nazir despite allegations that he had used AI, and the withdrawal of Canadian-Haitian author Thélyson Orélien from France’s top literary award, the Goncourt, over allegations he used AI for his first novel, which he denies . Following the publication of her article last month, Vara had told BBC’s Front Row programme that every other previous Caine Prize winning story she had put through Pangram “came out as 100% human”. The backlash on social media included comments from African writers with suggestions that such accusations are primarily being made against non-white writers.Wakatama said the Caine Prize organisation had considered Vara’s allegations “carefully and fairly”. “We chose to take a human-centred approach to the investigation. Our review included interviews with the author, the 2026 judging panel, and the Shallow Tales Review, where the story was first published,” she said. “It also included independent and expert-led metadata analysis of drafts written by the author.” In a statement, the Caine Prize explained further that the analysis had been conducted by an independent cyber security and digital forensic investigator . The day after winning the prestigious Caine Prize award earlier in October, Kundizeza had told the BBC he was inspired after hearing a poem read by South African Vangile Gantsho at an event in Ghana last year about her father’s obsession with building fish tanks. He said he had weaved that with fictionalised details from his own life around 2002 when Zimbabwe’s economic troubles began.

items.title: Maroc-Niger : la vente des billets débute jeudi
items.description: La Fédération royale marocaine de football (FRMF) annonce le lancement, jeudi 12 novembre 2026 à 12h00, de la vente des billets pour le match entre le Maroc et le Niger, prévu le mardi 17 novembre à 20h00 au Stade Prince Moulay Abdellah de Rabat, dans le cadre des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. La vente sera exclusivement accessible via la plateforme électronique Webook, ainsi que son application officielle. Les tarifs ont été fixés comme suit : Catégorie 3 : 100 DH Catégorie 2 : 200 DH Catégorie 1 : 300 DH Salon d’hospitalité : 1.000 DH Tribune VIP : 1.500 DH Tribune VVIP : 2.000 DH Skybox : 20.000 DH Pour les détenteurs de billets des catégories 1, 2 et 3, les billets seront directement transmis via l’application officielle Webook et permettront un accès direct au stade. Concernant les espaces d’hospitalité, VIP, VVIP et Skybox, des points spécifiques seront mis en place pour le retrait des Pass-Parking. Leurs emplacements seront communiqués ultérieurement par le comité d’organisation. La FRMF rappelle par ailleurs que le billet constitue l’unique moyen d’accès au stade, y compris pour les enfants accompagnant leurs parents. Les supporters sont également invités à respecter les consignes d’organisation ainsi que les numéros de sièges indiqués sur leurs billets. Le comité d’organisation prévient enfin que tout manquement à ces règles peut exposer son auteur aux mesures légales en vigueur. Tomates : un virus ravage les cultures et fait chuter la production
items.description: La raréfaction des tomates sur le marché marocain s'explique notamment par une forte contraction des superficies cultivées et les dégâts provoqués par un virus qui affecte les rendements. Le ministre de l'Agriculture, Khalid Hatimy, a fait état d'une baisse de 50% des surfaces plantées et de pertes pouvant atteindre 30% de la récolte. Une situation qui fragilise une filière stratégique et pousse les autorités à revoir les mécanismes de production, d'approvisionnement et de commercialisation. La disponibilité des tomates sur le marché national est confrontée à des difficultés qui trouvent leur origine dans les exploitations agricoles. La propagation d'un virus affectant les cultures, la réduction des superficies plantées et les contraintes liées à la production figurent parmi les principaux facteurs avancés par le gouvernement pour expliquer les tensions actuelles sur cette denrée. Intervenant mercredi devant la Commission des secteurs productifs à la Chambre des représentants, à l'occasion de la présentation du budget sectoriel de son département, le ministre de l'Agriculture, de la Pêche maritime et de la Souveraineté alimentaire, Khalid Hatimy, a livré plusieurs éléments sur la situation de la filière. Selon les chiffres qu'il a présentés, les superficies consacrées à la tomate ont diminué d'environ 50%, tandis qu'un virus entraîne des pertes estimées à 30% de la récolte. Le ministre a également évoqué une baisse de la production, passée de 250 à environ 150 tonnes selon les données communiquées lors de son intervention. Il a mis en garde contre le risque d'une aggravation de la situation si aucune solution n'est trouvée dans les trois prochaines années. « Si nous ne trouvons pas de solution à ce problème dans les trois ans, nous nous retrouverons face à une situation sans issue » , a-t-il averti. Une culture particulièrement vulnérable La tomate présente des contraintes spécifiques qui rendent son approvisionnement sensible aux variations de production. Khalid Hatimy a rappelé que cette culture ne peut être stockée ou conservée pendant de longues périodes. Elle repose sur différents cycles, certains s'étendant sur six mois, d'autres sur sept, avec des productions aussi bien sous serre qu'en plein champ. Cette dépendance aux calendriers de culture et aux conditions de production complique la gestion des volumes disponibles tout au long de l'année. Une baisse des rendements ou des superficies cultivées peut ainsi se répercuter rapidement sur les quantités commercialisées et, par conséquent, sur les prix. Face à cette situation, le ministère affirme travailler sur un programme destiné à résoudre les difficultés sanitaires de la filière. Le ministre a évoqué une solution technique qui permettrait de produire entre 600 et 700 hectares par an, sans toutefois détailler davantage, dans son intervention, les modalités de sa mise en œuvre. © Mounir Mehimdate Le marché national face à la concurrence extérieure Les difficultés de la filière s'inscrivent également dans un environnement commercial sous pression. Le ministre a évoqué la concurrence des marchés africains pour les produits marocains, ainsi que les pressions exercées par le marché européen sur la tomate. Il a notamment souligné que les exportations vers l'Europe reposaient sur des contrats clairement établis, tandis que les circuits commerciaux vers certains marchés africains présentaient davantage de difficultés, notamment concernant la déclaration de l'origine des marchandises. Ces tensions commerciales interviennent alors que les autorités cherchent à préserver les quantités nécessaires à l'approvisionnement du marché intérieur. Les dernières mesures gouvernementales ont ainsi conduit à restreindre les exportations de tomates, d'oignons et de pommes de terre vers les marchés africains, dans un contexte de tensions sur les disponibilités et les prix. Les restrictions ne constituent toutefois pas une explication de la baisse de production : elles relèvent de la réponse apportée par les autorités aux difficultés d'approvisionnement. La souveraineté alimentaire au cœur des arbitrages Pour le ministre, la question des exportations doit être précédée d'une évaluation précise des besoins nationaux. Il a appelé à définir une liste des produits essentiels, leur niveau de disponibilité et les quantités nécessaires à la consommation intérieure. « On ne peut pas ouvrir le projet à l'exportation sans déterminer les quantités que nous exporterons après avoir satisfait les besoins du marché national » , a-t-il déclaré, plaidant pour un encadrement légal du panier des produits de première nécessité. Cette orientation vise à éviter que les débouchés extérieurs ne se développent au détriment de l'approvisionnement local, particulièrement lorsque la production connaît des difficultés. © Mounir Mehimdate L'eau et la main-d'œuvre, autres défis de la filière Au-delà de la crise actuelle, le ministère prévoit une évaluation globale du secteur agricole dans le cadre d'une réflexion stratégique portant sur les horizons 2035 et 2050. Ce travail, qui devrait durer entre deux et trois mois, sera conduit filière par filière et examinera notamment les ressources humaines, le foncier, l'eau, la commercialisation, les aides publiques et la gouvernance. Les vingt contrats-programmes conclus dans le secteur feront également l'objet d'une évaluation individuelle. La gestion de l'eau constitue l'un des axes majeurs de cette réflexion. Khalid Hatimy a évoqué la mobilisation des ressources des barrages au profit de l'agriculture et le recours aux stations de dessalement, avec un volume annoncé de 1,7 milliard de mètres cubes. Il a insisté sur la nécessité de donner aux agriculteurs une visibilité préalable sur les quantités d'eau dont ils pourront disposer avant tout investissement. La disponibilité de la main-d'œuvre, l'amélioration de ses conditions de travail et le recours à la mécanisation figurent également parmi les défis identifiés pour renforcer la compétitivité des exploitations. The post Tomates : un virus ravage les cultures et fait chuter la production appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : cri du cœur des petits commerces
items.description: Pendant que les JOJ font vibrer Dakar, la désillusion s'installe aux abords du stade Iba Mar Diop. Loin de la fête, les petits commerçants jouent au chat et à la souris avec les forces de sécurité. Interdictions de vendre et confiscations de matériel rythment désormais leur quotidien. Dakar accueille les Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse (JOJ) depuis le 31 octobre. La fête bat son plein, le placard se remplit de médailles : un heureux événement pour toute une nation.Mais du côté des petits commerces installés aux alentours du site Iba Mar Diop, c’est le désenchantement et la désillusion. À deux jours de la clôture des Jeux, l'ambiance est tout autre aux abords du stade. Pour les petits commerces et les vendeurs de rue, contrairement aux disciplines sportives qui se jouent à l'intérieur des sites, c’est à un jeu de cache-cache qu’ils jouent avec les forces de l’ordre. S’ils s’étaient pourtant bien préparés à tirer profit de cet événement, c’est au fil des compétitions que leur enthousiasme s’est évaporé. Installée au coin d’une boutique, Hawa Diallo, vendeuse de beignets, avoue être déçue de la tournure de ces JOJ :« J’espérais que mon petit commerce allait être florissant vu l’affluence, mais je n’ai eu que déception. Parfois ça marche quand il y a de la masse, mais cet évènement n'a aucun effet sur mon commerce. » Un carton fait office de barrière autour de son fourneau, sur lequel une poêle profonde remplie d’huile frémit. Juste à côté, dans un bocal, quelques beignets s'entassent. Elle réajuste son foulard et confie ce qui la pousse à tenir malgré les difficultés .« J’ai 5 enfants et j’ai perdu mon mari. Du coup, pour éviter de mendier et de faire autre chose, je suis obligée de tenir ce business. Avec un bénéfice de 500 F, je pourrai au moins leur chercher de quoi manger», avoue-t-elle d'un air peiné. Tout juste à côté, une dame est assise, un sourire au coin des lèvres, témoin silencieuse de la discussion.Assise avec une petite sacoche en bandoulière, aucune glacière posée devant elle, ni de sachet d’eau visible. La raison ? Ils ont interdiction formelle de vendre aux alentours des sites. Fatou Sarr, supportée par une brique en ciment, n’attendait que cette occasion pour s’engouffrer dans la brèche et vider son sac :« Quand on organise un événement de ce genre, on doit impliquer toutes les couches de la société. Imagine, tu organises un événement pareil et des jeunes prennent le large… Nous, les vendeurs ambulants, nous ne profitons aucunement de ces jeux. » Toujours dans ses explications, elle affirme avoir été victime de déguerpissement :« J’avais un plateau rempli de bonbons qu’ils ont confisqué, et jusque-là je ne sais même plus où il est, ils ne me l’ont jamais rendu. » Interrogée sur la manière dont elle écoule ses sachets d’eau, elle répond :« On vend, mais dès qu’on voit leur voiture, on s’en va, au risque qu’ils confisquent nos marchandises. » Pour des solutions concrètes Fatou Sarr dénonce un traitement inégal et propose des solutions concrètes :« À l’intérieur, il y a des vendeurs, ils ont leurs tentes là-bas. Mais c’est une affaire de bras long? Ils les ont alloué comme bon leur semble.Mais imagine une famille qui vient regarder les activités : une bouteille d’eau qu’on vend à 100 F ici, eux ils la triplent ! Une famille composée de 5 personnes ne peut pas en acheter pour chacun, c’est trop cher. Le mieux était d’ériger des tentes ici pour ceux qui sont dehors. » Elle n’a pas manqué de conter une mésaventure vécue par l’une de ses camarades vendeuses .« Un jour, une vendeuse voulait entrer vendre à l’intérieur. Ils lui ont fait acheter un ticket, mais à la porte, ils lui ont demandé de déposer son plateau pour la laisser entrer les mains vides», témoigne-t-elle. Toujours sur la même allée, en face du site Iba Mar Diop, alors que les spectateurs commencent à affluer, Mamadiou Dia tient son petit business. Vendeur de café et de thé, il sert un client tout en veillant sur la théière posée sur son fourneau :« Vous voyez mon parasol posé à côté ? Je ne peux même pas l’installer parce qu’on peut nous déguerpir à tout moment. C’est hier que je suis revenu ici. Je m’étais installé là-bas derrière cette table » (il pointe du doigt une table installée dans une ruelle), « ils avaient confisqué toutes mes affaires. »Il affirme s’être préparé à accueillir les JOJ, mais n’en récolte que de la déception :« Avant que les jeux ne commencent, je croyais vraiment qu’on allait y trouver notre compte, mais hélas… Avec ce que nous vivons là, c’est même avant les jeux qu’on s’en sortait le mieux. » Fatou NGOM

items.title: Mbappe ruled out of France’s Nations League game against Italy
items.description: France’s captain Kylian Mbappe will miss his country’s Nations League match against Italy with a hamstring problem, coach Zinedine Zidane said Wednesday. Les Bleus take on Roberto Mancini’s Italy in Milan on Thursday as they bid to strengthen their grip on top spot in Group A1, before facing Turkey in Bordeaux on Sunday. “He will miss tomorrow, he felt a little pain and we won’t take any risk,” said Zidane. “It’s a shame to lose players but it’s part of the game. I hope that it’s nothing too serious and that he’ll be available for Sunday… It’s just a minor issue.” The Real Madrid forward is back in the France squad for this camp after missing their last three matches through injury. He has already netted 17 goals in all competitions for his club this season. Mbappe scored the winning goal in Zidane’s first match as coach, against Turkey in September in the Nations League, but had to leave the pitch shortly afterwards due to pain in his left knee. After three wins and a draw in four group games, victory over Italy would see France qualify for the quarter-finals. items.title: Otu dissolves Task Force over demolition of private property in Calabar
items.description: By Ike Uchechukwu Cross River State Governor, Sen Bassey Otu, has dissolved the State Planning and Development Control Task Force and ordered compensation for the owner of a nearly completed building its personnel pulled down. The Governor who described the action as an abuse of power said it was a assault on the rights of a citizen. In a press statement issued in Calabar on Wednesday by his Chief Press Secretary, Mr. Linus Obogo, the governor described the demolition as brazen, unconscionable and reprehensible. Governor Otu held the Task Force accountable for what the statement called gross team failure, and directed the immediate suspension of further demolition activities on the affected property. He also ordered the payment of compensation for the damage caused by the demolition. “Alleged violations of physical planning regulations cannot constitute a license for lawlessness,” the governor said. “No public institution can arrogate to itself powers that trample upon the rights and dignity of citizens.” According to him, such high-handedness, impunity and administrative recklessness are incompatible with the philosophy of his administration. “No individual, irrespective of position or institutional authority, enjoys the privilege of exercising public power recklessly, vindictively or outside the boundaries of established law and due process,” Otu stated. The governor warned that his administration would not tolerate official misconduct in any form. “My administration will neither shield, excuse nor reward official misconduct under any guise,” he declared. “Public office is a solemn trust, not an instrument of intimidation or oppression.” He directed all government agencies to operate with discipline, restraint, professionalism and the utmost respect for the rights of the people. “Under my watch, government will protect citizens and residents, uphold justice and insist that accountability remains non-negotiable,” the governor said. Checks by Vanguard showed that the demolished building located along parliamentary extension ,boulevard axis calabar Municipality Local Government Area in Calabar . Further Checks also showed that the building in question belongs to Mr Olajide Jamil who runs the popular Cent Apartment , and reportedly brought in investors from the United States of America to invest in real estate in Cross River State The post Otu dissolves Task Force over demolition of private property in Calabar appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Transport routier : nouvelle tranche de soutien pour la période du 1er au 15 novembre
items.description: Le ministère du Transport et de la Logistique a annoncé, mercredi, le lancement d'une nouvelle tranche de soutien exceptionnel direct au profit des professionnels du transport routier de personnes et de marchandises au titre de la période allant du 1er au 15 novembre. Dans un communiqué, le ministère indique que cette décision s'inscrit dans le cadre de l'accompagnement continu des professionnels du secteur du transport routier de personnes et de marchandises, ainsi que dans le sillage des mesures gouvernementales destinées à atténuer les répercussions de la hausse persistante des cours des produits pétroliers. Cette opération, explique-t-on, intervient également dans le cadre de la poursuite du soutien exceptionnel octroyé aux professionnels du transport routier « afin de contribuer à alléger les effets de l'augmentation des prix des carburants ». items.title: Many education reforms driven by personal preferences, not public demand – Prof Ayeetey
items.description: Professor of Development Economics at the Institute of Statistical, Social and Economic Research (ISSER) of the University of Ghana, Professor Ernest Ayeetey, has criticised the approach to education reforms in Ghana, saying that many changes are driven by the personal preferences of individuals rather than broad stakeholder consultations. He said some reforms were introduced after policymakers and officials became impressed by education systems they encountered during international conferences and engagements, without sufficient public discussion or evidence of the need for such changes. Speaking at the Achimota Speaks event on Wednesday, November 11, Prof Ayeetey said education had experienced more changes than any other sector in the country, but questioned the reasoning behind several of the reforms. “Many of the changes that we’ve seen in education, and education has seen more changes than any other sector in this country. Many of the changes have been prompted by personal preferences,” he said. He explained that some individuals returned from international conferences with ideas picked up from other countries and pushed for their adoption in Ghana. “Individuals go to conferences, they sit by somebody from Malaysia, and the Malaysian tells them about how they are doing and is impressed. Now as soon as they return to Ghana, they start a memo to the minister, they start a memo to the chief director, and that’s how our changes are. They will push and push and push,” he said. According to him, such proposals often gained traction depending on how strongly their proponents advocated for them, rather than through broad public engagement on the country’s educational needs. Prof Ayeetey said he could not recall many education reforms that had been prompted by extensive community discussions or widespread dissatisfaction expressed by different stakeholders. “I don’t recall any change or reform that we’ve had in education apart from the movement from five years secondary school plus two years Six form, moving to the junior secondary school. “I don’t recall any change that was precipitated by large discussion in the community. That was precipitated by obvious dissatisfaction with what was working and different people, different stakeholders expressing their discomfort,” he added. He said that the absence of broad consultations and clear justification for reforms could help explain why repeated changes had not produced meaningful improvements in the education system. “It’s not surprising that the changes have not led to any meaningful outcomes, meaningful outcomes that we can all see as evidence of improvement. I haven’t seen any report that suggests that there have been any, but we’ve changed things so many times,” he said. Prof Ayeetey acknowledged that Ghana had introduced several major education policies over the years, including Free Compulsory Universal Basic Education (FCUBE) in 1996, the establishment of the Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFund) in 2000, the education reforms of 2007 and 2008, the Free Senior High School policy and the more recent No-Fees-Stress policy. He noted that the introduction of reforms was not new to Ghana, but maintained that the processes through which decisions were made deserved closer scrutiny. He said the country needed to pay greater attention to the reasoning, consultations and evidence underpinning education policy changes to ensure they translated into measurable improvements.

items.title: Arrestation du principal auteur d’une violente agression avec viol et séquestration
items.description: Le suspect principal dans l'affaire d'agression sexuelle, violence et séquestration d'un jeune homme à Kerch El Ghaba a été arrêté et placé en détention. Les services de la brigade de la police judiciaire d'El Omrane charhés de l'enquête, sont parvenu à faire toute la lumière sur cette affaire d'une grande violence survenue dans ledit quartier au nord de Tunis. Selon les éléments de l'enquête rapportés par Mosaïque FM citant une source proche du dossier, un jeune homme a été agressé à l'arme blanche, puis séquestré s à l'intérieur d'un commerce de fruits secs, où il a été vicrile d'une agression sexuelle répétée. Souffrant de plusieurs blessures, la victime avait été prise en charge à l'hôpital de La Rabta de Tunis, rappelle la même source. Les investigations menées par la brigade précitée, ont permis d'identifier deux suspects déjà connus des services de police pour des faits similaires. La police a mis la main sur le suspect principal lors d'une descente, alors que son complice est parvenu à prendre la fuite. Sur instruction du ministère public près le tribunal de première instance de Tunis, le suspect interpellé a été placé en détention et un avis de recherche a été lancé à l'encontre du fugitif. Y. N. L’article Arrestation du principal auteur d'une violente agression avec viol et séquestration est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Stream accélère à l’export : la vision du géant de l’électronique algérien
items.description: Bomare Company veut changer d'échelle. Le fabricant algérien de téléviseurs Stream a annoncé un contrat portant sur 500.000 appareils pour le premier trimestre 2027, lors de son deuxième Afterwork avec la presse, organisé le 9 novembre à Alger. Présente à l'international depuis 2007, l'entreprise capitalise sur près de 20 ans d'expérience à l'exportation pour renforcer sa compétitivité et accélérer son développement sur les marchés extérieurs. Placée sous le thème « L'export comme levier d'excellence industrielle », cette deuxième rencontre s'inscrit dans une série de rendez-vous avec les médias. Après un premier échange consacré à la maîtrise industrielle et technologique, Bomare Company a choisi d'ouvrir le débat sur les normes internationales, l'innovation et les contraintes de l'export. L'occasion de répondre à diverses questions et de présenter ses résultats. Source : DR De l'importation à la fabrication… Le pari réussi d'Ali Boumediene Le parcours de Bomare Company commence par une rupture. Son fondateur et PDG, Ali Boumediene, exerçait dès 1992 dans l'importation et la distribution d'équipements électroniques et électroménagers, un secteur alors particulièrement rentable. En 2000, il choisit pourtant de privilégier la production. C'est ainsi que Bomare Company voit le jour en 2001 et se lance à l'international six ans plus tard, en 2007. Aujourd'hui, l’entreprise revendique plus de 1.000 collaborateurs, deux sites de production et un taux d'intégration locale de 45 %. L'enjeu, insiste son dirigeant, n'est pas seulement d'assembler des produits, mais de créer davantage de valeur en Algérie. Il résume d'ailleurs cette logique par un simple calcul : « On importe 55 $ pour un produit, et on exporte 100 $ ». Cette orientation s'appuie notamment sur la fabrication de cartes électroniques, la sous-traitance et les compétences locales. Elle repose aussi sur une organisation financière particulière. « Chaque année, les résultats réalisés par l'entreprise sont réinjectés dans son activité afin de financer de nouveaux investissements et de poursuivre son développement industriel… À ce jour, nous n'avons pas envisagé d'ouvrir le capital de l'entreprise », précise Ali Boumediene à TSA Algérie. Source : DR Une usine pensée et dimensionnée pour les marchés extérieurs La nouvelle usine de la marque à Blida doit donner une autre ampleur à cette stratégie. Selon Bomare Company, sa capacité pourrait dépasser 3 millions de téléviseurs par an. L'entreprise affiche l'objectif de destiner plus de 85 % de sa production à l'exportation, notamment grâce au développement de sa marque STREAM et à des coopérations industrielles de type OEM et ODM. Lors de la rencontre, un premier contrat portant sur 500.000 téléviseurs pour le premier trimestre 2027 a été évoqué. Quant au chiffre d'affaires annoncé, il est compris entre 12 et 15 millions de dollars. Pour Ali Boumediene, le repositionnement de certaines usines asiatiques vers l'automobile et les énergies renouvelables devrait ouvrir des perspectives à l'industrie algérienne de l'électroménager. « Nous disposons de plusieurs atouts : des ressources énergétiques, une main-d'œuvre compétitive et des compétences humaines importantes », expose-t-il. L'Europe, un test grandeur nature vers l'excellence industrielle L'expérience de l'export n'a pas été sans obstacles. Entre 2007 et 2015, rappelle le PDG, « des conteneurs de produits pouvaient rester immobilisés jusqu'à 45 jours au port d'Alger ». L'introduction progressive de facilités douanières à partir de 2012, à l'instar de la déclaration des marchandises à l'usine, a contribué à alléger certaines contraintes. Mais pour l'entreprise, la concurrence se joue aussi sur le respect des normes : « Avant de parler de compétitivité, il faut d'abord respecter les normes internationales, investir dans la recherche et suivre les évolutions des marchés ». Pour vendre en Europe, Bomare Company met en avant sa démarche de conformité au marquage CE, à la réglementation RoHS et aux exigences de réparabilité et de durabilité en France (6,8/10). « Notre priorité actuelle est le marché européen, et ce choix répond à une stratégie bien précise », exprime le responsable. L'Allemagne, qui représente un marché de plus de 12 millions de téléviseurs, tient une place centrale, tant pour son potentiel commercial que pour les exigences de ses consommateurs. L'expérience acquise par Bomare Company sur ce marché devra ensuite servir de tremplin vers l'Afrique. SAV et formations : les autres leviers de l'expansion de Bomare Company Pour s'imposer sur les marchés internationaux, Bomare Company ne mise pas uniquement sur la vente de ses produits, mais aussi sur la qualité de son service client. L'entreprise a présenté une activité de réparation de téléviseurs STREAM et d'autres marques lancée en 2026. Et dès décembre, l'assistant virtuel Streamy, chatbot développé en Algérie et fondé sur l'IA, doit accompagner les clients européens 24h/24. La marque met aussi en avant une garantie de 5 ans pour ses produits, « exactement comme en Algérie », et étudie la mise en place d'un dispositif de service après-vente en Allemagne. En parallèle, Bomare Company multiplie les passerelles avec le monde universitaire, notamment avec l'université de Blida, et développe son propre programme de formation ElectroSkills. « L'objectif n'est pas uniquement de communiquer, mais aussi de sensibiliser les jeunes et de leur faire découvrir les réalités du monde industriel », souligne Ali Boumediene. Après l'Europe, le groupe envisage de s'implanter davantage en Afrique : « Notre ambition est d'aller au-delà de la simple exportation de produits finis. Nous envisageons progressivement d'installer des unités d'assemblage directement dans certains pays africains », conclut le dirigeant. L’article Stream accélère à l'export : la vision du géant de l'électronique algérien est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Mahama pushes for expanded economic cooperation with India, Lebanon
items.description: President John Mahama has called for stronger economic and diplomatic relations between Ghana and India and Lebanon, highlighting opportunities for expanded trade, investment and development cooperation. He made the remarks on Wednesday, November 11, when he received Letters of Credence from several ambassadors, including the new South African High Commissioner to Ghana at the Jubilee House in Accra. Welcoming India’s High Commissioner to Ghana, Surendra Bhagat, President Mahama described relations between the two countries as warm and long-standing, noting India’s contribution to Ghana’s development over the years. He said the relationship was built on shared principles, including South-South cooperation, anti-colonial solidarity, the Commonwealth and the Non-Aligned Movement. The President also commended Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi for what he described as the transformation taking place in India. He recalled Mr Modi’s visit to Ghana in 2025, saying it provided an opportunity for both countries to elevate their relations to a comprehensive partnership. President Mahama cited the memorandum of understanding signed between the University of Ghana and the Zoological Survey of India on academic and scientific cooperation as one of the important outcomes of the visit. He also acknowledged India’s support for Ghana’s socio-economic development through concessional financing, lines of credit, grants and technical cooperation. “I assure you, High Commissioner, of Ghana’s readiness to work closely with you to further deepen the excellent relations between our two countries,” he said. Turning to Lebanon’s new Ambassador, Fouad Kazaka, President Mahama congratulated him on his appointment and assured him of the government’s cooperation. He recognised the contribution of the Lebanese community to Ghana’s development, particularly in manufacturing, commerce, real estate, education, health and hospitality. The President urged the Ambassador to work with Ghana’s business community to expand trade and investment, identifying agri-processing, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, infrastructure, renewable energy, information technology and tourism as areas with potential for cooperation. On the situation in the Middle East, President Mahama welcomed the trilateral peace framework brokered by the United States and signed by Lebanon and Israel on June 26, 2026. He expressed optimism that the agreement would bring a lasting end to hostilities and restore Lebanon’s sovereignty. “I am optimistic that the agreement will lead to a permanent end to hostilities and the restoration of Lebanon’s sovereignty,” he said.
